17:54.ar: رَّبُّكُمۡ أَعۡلَمُ بِكُمۡۖ إِن يَشَأۡ يَرۡحَمۡكُمۡ أَوۡ إِن يَشَأۡ يُعَذِّبۡكُمۡۚ وَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَٰكَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَكِيلࣰ ا
17:54.en: Your Lord is Best Aware of you. If He will, He will have mercy on you, or if He will, He will punish you. We have not sent thee (O Muhammad) as a warden over them

73:9.ar: رَّبُّ ٱلۡمَشۡرِقِ وَٱلۡمَغۡرِبِ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ فَٱتَّخِذۡهُ وَكِيلࣰ ا
73:9.en: Lord of the East and the West; there is no Allah save Him; so choose thou Him alone for thy defender

11:123.ar: وَلِلَّهِ غَيۡبُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَإِلَيۡهِ يُرۡجَعُ ٱلۡأَمۡرُ كُلُّهُۥ فَٱعۡبُدۡهُ وَتَوَكَّلۡ عَلَيۡهِۚ وَمَا رَبُّكَ بِغَٰفِلٍ عَمَّا تَعۡمَلُونَ
11:123.en: And Allah's is the Invisible of the heavens and the earth, and unto Him the whole matter will be returned. So worship Him and put thy trust in Him. Lo! thy Lord is not unaware of what ye (mortals) do

6:102.ar: ذَٰلِكُمُ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّكُمۡۖ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَۖ خَٰلِقُ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ فَٱعۡبُدُوهُۚ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ وَكِيلࣱ‏
6:102.en: Such is Allah, your Lord. There is no Allah save Him, the Creator of all things, so worship Him. And He taketh care of all things

65:3.ar: وَيَرۡزُقۡهُ مِنۡ حَيۡثُ لَا يَحۡتَسِبُۚ وَمَن يَتَوَكَّلۡ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَهُوَ حَسۡبُهُۥٓۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بَٰلِغُ أَمۡرِهِۦۚ قَدۡ جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لِكُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدۡرࣰ ا
65:3.en: And will provide for him from (a quarter) whence he hath no expectation. And whosoever putteth his trust in Allah, He will suffice him. Lo! Allah bringeth His command to pass. Allah hath set a measure for all things

26:217.en: And put thy trust in the Mighty, the Merciful

26:218.en: Who seeth thee when thou standest up (to pray)

26:219.en: And (seeth) thine abasement among those who fall prostrate (in worship)

26:220.en: Lo! He, only He, is the Hearer, the Knower

25:58.ar: وَتَوَكَّلۡ عَلَى ٱلۡحَيِّ ٱلَّذِي لَا يَمُوتُ وَسَبِّحۡ بِحَمۡدِهِۦۚ وَكَفَىٰ بِهِۦ بِذُنُوبِ عِبَادِهِۦ خَبِيرًا
25:58.en: And trust thou in the Living One Who dieth not, and hymn His praise. He sufficeth as the Knower of His bondmen's sins

9:129.ar: فَإِن تَوَلَّوۡاْ فَقُلۡ حَسۡبِيَ ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَۖ عَلَيۡهِ تَوَكَّلۡتُۖ وَهُوَ رَبُّ ٱلۡعَرۡشِ ٱلۡعَظِيمِ
9:129.en: Now, if they turn away (O Muhammad) say: Allah sufficeth me. There is no Allah save Him. In Him have I put my trust, and He is Lord of the Tremendous Throne

3:173.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ قَالَ لَهُمُ ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّ ٱلنَّاسَ قَدۡ جَمَعُواْ لَكُمۡ فَٱخۡشَوۡهُمۡ فَزَادَهُمۡ إِيمَٰنࣰ ا وَقَالُواْ حَسۡبُنَا ٱللَّهُ وَنِعۡمَ ٱلۡوَكِيلُ
3:173.en: Those unto whom men said: Lo! the people have gathered against you, therefor fear them. (The threat of danger) but increased the faith of them and they cried: Allah is Sufficient for us! Most Excellent is He in Whom we trust

21:69.ar: قُلۡنَا يَٰنَارُ كُونِي بَرۡدࣰ ا وَسَلَٰمًا عَلَىٰٓ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ
21:69.en: We said: O fire, be coolness and peace for Abraham

17:2.ar: وَءَاتَيۡنَا مُوسَى ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَجَعَلۡنَٰهُ هُدࣰ ى لِّبَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ أَلَّا تَتَّخِذُواْ مِن دُونِي وَكِيلࣰ ا
17:2.en: We gave unto Moses the Scripture, and We appointed it a guidance for the children of Israel, saying: Choose no guardian beside Me

5:22.ar: قَالُواْ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّ فِيهَا قَوۡمࣰ ا جَبَّارِينَ وَإِنَّا لَن نَّدۡخُلَهَا حَتَّىٰ يَخۡرُجُواْ مِنۡهَا فَإِن يَخۡرُجُواْ مِنۡهَا فَإِنَّا دَٰخِلُونَ
5:22.en: They said: O Moses! Lo! a giant people (dwell) therein and lo! we go not in till they go forth from thence. When they go forth from thence, then we will enter (not till then)

5:23.ar: قَالَ رَجُلَانِ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخَافُونَ أَنۡعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِمَا ٱدۡخُلُواْ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡبَابَ فَإِذَا دَخَلۡتُمُوهُ فَإِنَّكُمۡ غَٰلِبُونَۚ وَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَتَوَكَّلُوٓاْ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
5:23.en: Then out spake two of those who feared (their Lord, men) unto whom Allah had been gracious: Enter in upon them by the gate, for if ye enter by it, lo! ye will be victorious. So put your trust (in Allah) if ye are indeed believers

5:24.ar: قَالُواْ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّا لَن نَّدۡخُلَهَآ أَبَدࣰ ا مَّا دَامُواْ فِيهَا فَٱذۡهَبۡ أَنتَ وَرَبُّكَ فَقَٰتِلَآ إِنَّا هَٰهُنَا قَٰعِدُونَ
5:24.en: They said: O Moses! We will never enter (the land) while they are in it. So go thou and thy Lord and fight! We will sit here

17:86.ar: وَلَئِن شِئۡنَا لَنَذۡهَبَنَّ بِٱلَّذِيٓ أَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ ثُمَّ لَا تَجِدُ لَكَ بِهِۦ عَلَيۡنَا وَكِيلًا
17:86.en: And if We willed We could withdraw that which We have revealed unto thee, then wouldst thou find no guardian for thee against Us in respect thereof

9:40.ar: إِلَّا تَنصُرُوهُ فَقَدۡ نَصَرَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِذۡ أَخۡرَجَهُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ ثَانِيَ ٱثۡنَيۡنِ إِذۡ هُمَا فِي ٱلۡغَارِ إِذۡ يَقُولُ لِصَٰحِبِهِۦ لَا تَحۡزَنۡ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَنَاۖ فَأَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُۥ عَلَيۡهِ وَأَيَّدَهُۥ بِجُنُودࣲ لَّمۡ تَرَوۡهَا وَجَعَلَ كَلِمَةَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ ٱلسُّفۡلَىٰۗ وَكَلِمَةُ ٱللَّهِ هِيَ ٱلۡعُلۡيَاۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ
9:40.en: If ye help him not, still Allah helped him when those who disbelieve drove him forth, the second of two; when they two were in the cave, when he said unto his comrade: Grieve not. Lo! Allah is with us. Then Allah caused His peace of reassurance to descend upon him and supported him with hosts ye cannot see, and made the word of those who disbelieved the nethermost, while Allah's Word it was that became the uppermost. Allah is Mighty, Wise

b7XvXiJR4HI.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: Names of Support and Aid, Al-Wakeel (The Trustee)
b7XvXiJR4HI.one_line: Al-Wakil presents Himself for you to appoint as trustee; tawakkul means full effort, heart reliance and accepting the result, as in the Hijrah plan.
b7XvXiJR4HI.summary: He presents Al-Wakil, the One who takes charge of His servants' affairs, as a name you choose to affiliate with, unlike Al-Wali where Allah must choose you. That is why the Quran almost always introduces it with verses of self-description, like a notary checking that you trust someone with power of attorney who has experience, time and care for you. Allah presents Himself as Lord of East and West, Knower of the unseen, Ever-Living, who sees you in prayer, and asks you to take Him as trustee. Saying 'Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best trustee' is the signature on that contract, words of Ibrahim in the fire and of the companions threatened after Uhud. The hadith to Ibn Abbas sums up reliance, and Bani Israel's failure to enter Jerusalem shows its absence. Tawakkul, the most important internal act of worship, has three parts: exhausting your effort, relying in your heart that only Allah delivers results, and accepting whatever comes. The Prophet's meticulous Hijrah plan still failed at the cave, and Allah alone kept the pursuers from looking down; even at the Isra he tied the Buraq. Tawakkul gives courage for calculated risks, confidence that you are never alone, calm, and the acceptance that lets you keep getting up after failure.

outline.heading: Opening
Twelve times, always alone
outline.gist: Al-Wakil appears twelve times as a name and never paired; he opens the category of support and aid.

outline.heading: The One who takes charge of your affairs
outline.gist: Allah takes on the affairs of His servants, and you get to choose whether to affiliate with this name.

outline.heading: He presents Himself, you choose
outline.gist: Unlike Al-Wali, where Allah must choose you, here He presents Himself and the choice is yours; He nearly always introduces the name with self-praise.

outline.heading: Power of attorney
outline.gist: A notary asks whether you are sure before you hand someone power over your assets and decisions.

outline.heading: What you look for in a trustee
outline.gist: Experience and wisdom, time to focus on you, and genuine care; otherwise you put yourself in jeopardy.

outline.heading: Allah describes Himself before asking
outline.gist: Lord of the East and West, Knower of the unseen to whom all returns, Creator of everything: so take Him as trustee.

outline.heading: He suffices and reaches His aims
outline.gist: Whoever relies on Allah, He is enough; rely on the Mighty, the Merciful, who sees you standing and moving among those who prostrate.

outline.heading: The Ever-Living; enough for me
outline.gist: Rely on the One who never dies; if all turn away, say Allah suffices me, upon Him I rely.

outline.heading: Signing the contract
outline.gist: The companions told an army had gathered against them grew in faith and said Allah suffices us and He is the best trustee.

outline.heading: Ibrahim in the fire
outline.gist: Ibrahim said these words as he was catapulted into the fire, refusing Jibril's help; the fire became cool and he called those his best days.

outline.heading: The hadith to Ibn Abbas
outline.gist: Guard Allah's place in your heart and He guards you; ask Him and seek His help; no one can benefit or harm you except as He wills; the ink has dried.

outline.heading: Bani Israel never learned it
outline.gist: They were told to take no trustee but Allah yet could not enter Jerusalem; even the Prophet was warned he would find no trustee against Allah.

outline.heading: First: exhaust your effort
outline.gist: Tawakkul, the most important internal worship, needs full effort; not studying and then claiming tawakkul before an exam is not tawakkul.

outline.heading: Second: rely in your heart
outline.gist: Know that only Allah delivers results even if you know the material cover to cover; that balance is what Islam is.

outline.heading: Third: accept the result
outline.gist: Being disgruntled when you do not get what you worked for is not tawakkul; whatever He chooses, you are content.

outline.heading: The Hijrah plan
outline.gist: He slept outside for months so Ali in his bed seemed normal, left at noon in the opposite direction, had a shepherd erase their tracks and hid three days in a cave.

outline.heading: The plan failed at the cave
outline.gist: The pursuers stood at the cave entrance; Allah simply did not let them look down.

outline.heading: Two with Allah as their third
outline.gist: No one thought to look; the Prophet told Abu Bakr not to grieve because they had done their part and the result is Allah's.

outline.heading: Tying the Buraq
outline.gist: At Jerusalem he tied the Buraq sent by Allah, a reflex of always doing your part.

outline.heading: Living with it: courage
outline.gist: Negligence is not tawakkul; once you have done everything you can, you are not crippled by fear, which is not recklessness.

outline.heading: Calculated risks and confidence
outline.gist: Courage for calculated risks and walking the earth confident that you are never alone and your outcomes matter to Someone.

outline.heading: Calm and acceptance
outline.gist: Tawakkul brings the calm to decide well and the acceptance that lets you get up after every failure, since you do not know what is best for you.

7:32.ar: قُلۡ مَنۡ حَرَّمَ زِينَةَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّتِيٓ أَخۡرَجَ لِعِبَادِهِۦ وَٱلطَّيِّبَٰتِ مِنَ ٱلرِّزۡقِۚ قُلۡ هِيَ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ فِي ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا خَالِصَةࣰ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِۗ كَذَٰلِكَ نُفَصِّلُ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ لِقَوۡمࣲ يَعۡلَمُونَ
7:32.en: Say: Who hath forbidden the adornment of Allah which He hath brought forth for His bondmen, and the good things of His providing? Say: Such, on the Day of Resurrection, will be only for those who believed during the life of the world. Thus do we detail Our revelations for people who have knowledge

7:55.ar: ٱدۡعُواْ رَبَّكُمۡ تَضَرُّعࣰ ا وَخُفۡيَةًۚ إِنَّهُۥ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُعۡتَدِينَ
7:55.en: (O mankind!) Call upon your Lord humbly and in secret. Lo! He loveth not aggressors

7:56.ar: وَلَا تُفۡسِدُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ بَعۡدَ إِصۡلَٰحِهَا وَٱدۡعُوهُ خَوۡفࣰ ا وَطَمَعًاۚ إِنَّ رَحۡمَتَ ٱللَّهِ قَرِيبࣱ مِّنَ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
7:56.en: Work not confusion in the earth after the fair ordering (thereof). and call on Him in fear and hope. Lo! the mercy of Allah is nigh unto the good

7:146.ar: سَأَصۡرِفُ عَنۡ ءَايَٰتِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَتَكَبَّرُونَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ بِغَيۡرِ ٱلۡحَقِّ وَإِن يَرَوۡاْ كُلَّ ءَايَةࣲ لَّا يُؤۡمِنُواْ بِهَا وَإِن يَرَوۡاْ سَبِيلَ ٱلرُّشۡدِ لَا يَتَّخِذُوهُ سَبِيلࣰ ا وَإِن يَرَوۡاْ سَبِيلَ ٱلۡغَيِّ يَتَّخِذُوهُ سَبِيلࣰ اۚ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمۡ كَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا وَكَانُواْ عَنۡهَا غَٰفِلِينَ
7:146.en: I shall turn away from My revelations those who magnify themselves wrongfully in the earth, and if they see each token believe it not, and if they see the way of righteousness choose it nor for (their) way, and if they see the way of error choose if for (their) way. That is because they deny Our revelations and are used to disregard them

7:155.ar: وَٱخۡتَارَ مُوسَىٰ قَوۡمَهُۥ سَبۡعِينَ رَجُلࣰ ا لِّمِيقَٰتِنَاۖ فَلَمَّآ أَخَذَتۡهُمُ ٱلرَّجۡفَةُ قَالَ رَبِّ لَوۡ شِئۡتَ أَهۡلَكۡتَهُم مِّن قَبۡلُ وَإِيَّٰيَۖ أَتُهۡلِكُنَا بِمَا فَعَلَ ٱلسُّفَهَآءُ مِنَّآۖ إِنۡ هِيَ إِلَّا فِتۡنَتُكَ تُضِلُّ بِهَا مَن تَشَآءُ وَتَهۡدِي مَن تَشَآءُۖ أَنتَ وَلِيُّنَا فَٱغۡفِرۡ لَنَا وَٱرۡحَمۡنَاۖ وَأَنتَ خَيۡرُ ٱلۡغَٰفِرِينَ
7:155.en: And Moses chose of his people seventy men for Our appointed tryst and, when the trembling came on them, he said: My Lord! If Thou hadst willed Thou hadst destroyed them long before, and me with them. Wilt thou destroy us for that which the ignorant among us did? It is but Thy trial (of us). Thou sendest whom Thou wilt astray and guidest whom Thou wilt: Thou art our Protecting Friend, therefore forgive us and have mercy on us, Thou, the Best of all who show forgiveness

7:156.ar: ۞وَٱكۡتُبۡ لَنَا فِي هَٰذِهِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا حَسَنَةࣰ وَفِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ إِنَّا هُدۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَۚ قَالَ عَذَابِيٓ أُصِيبُ بِهِۦ مَنۡ أَشَآءُۖ وَرَحۡمَتِي وَسِعَتۡ كُلَّ شَيۡءࣲۚ فَسَأَكۡتُبُهَا لِلَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَ وَيُؤۡتُونَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱلَّذِينَ هُم بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
7:156.en: And ordain for us in this world that which is good, and in the Hereafter (that which is good), Lo! We have turned unto Thee. He said: I smite with My punishment whom I will, and My mercy embraceth all things, therefore I shall ordain it for those who ward off (evil) and pay the poor-due, and those who believe Our revelations

6:75.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ نُرِيٓ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ مَلَكُوتَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلِيَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُوقِنِينَ
6:75.en: Thus did We show Abraham the kingdom of the heavens and the earth that he might be of those possessing certainty

6:76.ar: فَلَمَّا جَنَّ عَلَيۡهِ ٱلَّيۡلُ رَءَا كَوۡكَبࣰ اۖ قَالَ هَٰذَا رَبِّيۖ فَلَمَّآ أَفَلَ قَالَ لَآ أُحِبُّ ٱلۡأٓفِلِينَ
6:76.en: When the night grew dark upon him he beheld a star. He said: This is my Lord. But when it set, he said: I love not things that set

6:77.ar: فَلَمَّا رَءَا ٱلۡقَمَرَ بَازِغࣰ ا قَالَ هَٰذَا رَبِّيۖ فَلَمَّآ أَفَلَ قَالَ لَئِن لَّمۡ يَهۡدِنِي رَبِّي لَأَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ

6:78.en: And when he saw the sun uprising, he cried: This is my Lord! This is greater! And when it set he exclaimed: O my people! Lo! I am free from all that ye associate (with Him)

6:79.ar: إِنِّي وَجَّهۡتُ وَجۡهِيَ لِلَّذِي فَطَرَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ حَنِيفࣰ اۖ وَمَآ أَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ

OLtoRA-BFTM.title: Ramadan 2024 Night 8: Quranic Reflections on Surat Al-A'raf
OLtoRA-BFTM.one_line: Al-A'raf on communal salvation and indifference: balanced dua tied to conduct, arrogance blocking guidance, all-embracing mercy, and the danger of declaring things haram.
OLtoRA-BFTM.summary: He reads Al-A'raf as the surah of communities: salvation is communal, and a society survives only if it rejects indifference and takes decisive stands. Western individualism tempts Muslims to see themselves apart from their community, but they are only as good as their treatment of its weakest, as the Prophet's parable of the ship shows. From 7:55-56 he teaches two balances in dua, public and private, fearful and hopeful, and argues that the command not to spread corruption sits between them because dua is worthless when one's life contradicts it, whether through haram income, abusing a spouse or neglecting parents. From 7:146 he names arrogance, even toward one person, and indifference as what turns hearts away from Allah's signs, and mocks waiting passively for the heart to open. From 7:156 he explains that Allah's mercy encompasses everything, distinguishing general and special mercy. Finally, 7:32 warns that forbidding what Allah allowed is as evil as permitting the forbidden: calling things haram out of fear cheapens a sacred word, holds societies back and drives many people out of the faith.

outline.heading: Opening
Why the relationship surahs come after the method
outline.gist: Al-An'am and Al-A'raf were revealed early but placed after the job and method so the relationship with Allah guides everything that came before.

outline.heading: Three dimensions of every surah
outline.gist: When it was revealed, where it sits in the mushaf, and what it does for you in your own time and place.

outline.heading: Salvation is the salvation of communities
outline.gist: The Quran offers sociological insight: communities survive only by rejecting indifference and being decisive about their relationship with Allah.

outline.heading: A surah of communities, story after story
outline.gist: Al-An'am has one personal story, Ibrahim reasoning from the stars; Al-A'raf tells of whole peoples who lost their chance through indifference.

outline.heading: Some surahs speak more to your context
outline.gist: It is encouraged that certain surahs mean more to you, and these two address struggles Muslims face daily.

outline.heading: Western individualism and indifference to community
outline.gist: Personal success means little if your society fails; we are only as good as our care for its most vulnerable.

outline.heading: The parable of the ship
outline.gist: If those on the lower deck drill a hole for water and no one stops them, everyone drowns.

outline.heading: This is your group, for better or worse
outline.gist: Even when you are not proud of the ummah, you must work with it, because we sail together or sink together.

outline.heading: Interlude
Dua openly and in secret
outline.gist: Supplicate visibly and audibly, with emotion showing, and also hidden between you and Allah.

outline.heading: Congregational dua as shared vulnerability
outline.gist: Ramadan night prayers fulfil the public side, where believers let themselves be vulnerable together; the private side must be built too.

outline.heading: Transgression is neglecting one of the two
outline.gist: Only private dua cuts you off from the community; only public dua leaves nothing between you and Allah.

outline.heading: Dua in fear and in hope
outline.gist: A second balance: fear of just punishment and longing for reward, with Allah's mercy near to those who excel.

outline.heading: Why corruption is forbidden between the dua commands
outline.gist: Dua cannot be separated from behaviour; it must match your plan, ethics and values.

outline.heading: The weary traveller fed on haram
outline.gist: A dishevelled traveller raising his hands has his dua rejected because his food, drink and clothing are unlawful.

outline.heading: Fix the corruption before the dua
outline.gist: A man who abuses his wife or a child who wrongs his parents gains nothing from tearful dua until the behaviour changes.

outline.heading: Turned away from the signs by unjust arrogance
outline.gist: There is never a right to arrogance; such people see every sign and still choose the wrong path because they turned from truth they recognised.

outline.heading: Indifference runs through the surah
outline.gist: Few people care fully; most care a little, or in waves like a tide, never enough to take a stand.

outline.heading: Arrogance toward even one person
outline.gist: Feeling better than a single human being closes the heart, because Allah's teachings enter only a humble heart.

outline.heading: Ask what is wrong with me
outline.gist: Someone who cares asks why the teachings are not entering his heart instead of waiting for change.

outline.heading: Waiting for a dream or for Allah to will it
outline.gist: Some expect a vision to fix them, or say it will happen when Allah wills, which borders on blaming Him.

outline.heading: Humble and committed hearts are brought back
outline.gist: Arrogant, indifferent hearts are steered away from the signs, while the humble are guided back.

outline.heading: The dua of those who returned to Allah
outline.gist: After their great error the people of Musa asked for good in both worlds and said they had returned to Him, the root of the name Yahud.

outline.heading: My mercy encompasses everything
outline.gist: Ar-Rahman and Ar-Rahim share one root: a mercy for every living thing and a special mercy for those who seek more of Him.

outline.heading: One hundred parts of mercy
outline.gist: Allah sent one part to earth, behind every act of compassion even among animals, and will join it to the other ninety-nine on the Last Day.

outline.heading: Special mercy for the mindful and the giving
outline.gist: Even Iblis is said to hope for mercy that day, but the special share is written for the mindful who give and believe in the signs.

outline.heading: Who dares forbid Allah's adornments
outline.gist: The verse challenges anyone who forbids the beautiful extras and lawful provision Allah brought out for His servants.

outline.heading: Forbidding the lawful is as evil as permitting the forbidden
outline.gist: Neither error is safer; most scholars of legal theory treat wrongly forbidding as the graver one.

outline.heading: The audacity of declaring haram
outline.gist: Only Allah may point at something and forbid it; doing so without certain evidence claims to know better than Him.

outline.heading: Long-term damage of false prohibitions
outline.gist: A century later people find it was never haram, whole fields have been abandoned, and Islam is blamed for holding societies back.

outline.heading: Televisions, satellite dishes and the internet
outline.gist: He recalls each technology being declared haram, then the same scholars owning them years later.

outline.heading: Haram means sacred
outline.gist: Throwing the word around like peanuts makes people stop respecting it, as a child told no to everything does everything.

outline.heading: Why many people leave the faith
outline.gist: In his experience a large share of those who leave were taught that disputed matters were undisputedly haram, and later cannot forgive it.

outline.heading: Haram only for what exclusively harms
outline.gist: Everything carries some risk; even smoking took scholars time and medical evidence before it was forbidden.

outline.heading: Fighting over haircuts opens the floodgates
outline.gist: Wasting the word on trivial matters means people eventually break loose and fall into what is truly forbidden.

outline.heading: Fear is never a reason to call something haram
outline.gist: The verse dares anyone to challenge Allah's authority; this is no licence to permit the forbidden, but fear of life is a bad motive.

4:66.ar: وَلَوۡ أَنَّا كَتَبۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ أَنِ ٱقۡتُلُوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۡ أَوِ ٱخۡرُجُواْ مِن دِيَٰرِكُم مَّا فَعَلُوهُ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣱ مِّنۡهُمۡۖ وَلَوۡ أَنَّهُمۡ فَعَلُواْ مَا يُوعَظُونَ بِهِۦ لَكَانَ خَيۡرࣰ ا لَّهُمۡ وَأَشَدَّ تَثۡبِيتࣰ ا
4:66.en: And if We had decreed for them: Lay down your lives or go forth from your dwellings, but few of them would have done it; though if they did what they are exhorted to do it would be better for them, and more strengthening

4:75.ar: وَمَا لَكُمۡ لَا تُقَٰتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡمُسۡتَضۡعَفِينَ مِنَ ٱلرِّجَالِ وَٱلنِّسَآءِ وَٱلۡوِلۡدَٰنِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَآ أَخۡرِجۡنَا مِنۡ هَٰذِهِ ٱلۡقَرۡيَةِ ٱلظَّالِمِ أَهۡلُهَا وَٱجۡعَل لَّنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ وَلِيࣰّ ا وَٱجۡعَل لَّنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ نَصِيرًا
4:75.en: How should ye not fight for the cause of Allah and of the feeble among men and of the women and the children who are crying: Our Lord! Bring us forth from out this town of which the people are oppressors! Oh, give us from thy presence some protecting friend! Oh, give us from Thy presence some defender

4:97.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ تَوَفَّىٰهُمُ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ ظَالِمِيٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ قَالُواْ فِيمَ كُنتُمۡۖ قَالُواْ كُنَّا مُسۡتَضۡعَفِينَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ قَالُوٓاْ أَلَمۡ تَكُنۡ أَرۡضُ ٱللَّهِ وَٰسِعَةࣰ فَتُهَاجِرُواْ فِيهَاۚ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ مَأۡوَىٰهُمۡ جَهَنَّمُۖ وَسَآءَتۡ مَصِيرًا
4:97.en: Lo! as for those whom the angels take (in death) while they wrong themselves, (the angels) will ask: In what were ye engaged? They will say: We were oppressed in the land. 4:98.ar: إِلَّا ٱلۡمُسۡتَضۡعَفِينَ مِنَ ٱلرِّجَالِ وَٱلنِّسَآءِ وَٱلۡوِلۡدَٰنِ لَا يَسۡتَطِيعُونَ حِيلَةࣰ وَلَا يَهۡتَدُونَ سَبِيلࣰ ا
4:98.en: Except the feeble among men, and the women, and the children, who are unable to devise a plan and are not shown a way

4:99.en: As for such, it may be that Allah will pardon them. Allah is ever Clement, Forgiving

4:135.ar: ۞يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُونُواْ قَوَّٰمِينَ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِ شُهَدَآءَ لِلَّهِ وَلَوۡ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِكُمۡ أَوِ ٱلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ وَٱلۡأَقۡرَبِينَۚ إِن يَكُنۡ غَنِيًّا أَوۡ فَقِيرࣰ ا فَٱللَّهُ أَوۡلَىٰ بِهِمَاۖ فَلَا تَتَّبِعُواْ ٱلۡهَوَىٰٓ أَن تَعۡدِلُواْۚ وَإِن تَلۡوُۥٓاْ أَوۡ تُعۡرِضُواْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ خَبِيرࣰ ا

Be ye staunch in justice, witnesses for Allah, even though it be against yourselves or (your) parents or (your) kindred, whether (the case be of) a rich man or a poor man, for Allah is nearer unto both (them ye are). 37:102.ar: فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ مَعَهُ ٱلسَّعۡيَ قَالَ يَٰبُنَيَّ إِنِّيٓ أَرَىٰ فِي ٱلۡمَنَامِ أَنِّيٓ أَذۡبَحُكَ فَٱنظُرۡ مَاذَا تَرَىٰۚ قَالَ يَٰٓأَبَتِ ٱفۡعَلۡ مَا تُؤۡمَرُۖ سَتَجِدُنِيٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
37:102.en: And when (his son) was old enough to walk with him, (Abraham) said: O my dear son, I have seen in a dream that I must sacrifice thee. So look, what thinkest thou? He said: O my father! Do that which thou art commanded. Allah willing, thou shalt find me of the steadfast

5:8.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُونُواْ قَوَّٰمِينَ لِلَّهِ شُهَدَآءَ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِۖ وَلَا يَجۡرِمَنَّكُمۡ شَنَـَٔانُ قَوۡمٍ عَلَىٰٓ أَلَّا تَعۡدِلُواْۚ ٱعۡدِلُواْ هُوَ أَقۡرَبُ لِلتَّقۡوَىٰۖ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ خَبِيرُۢ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ
5:8.en: O ye who believe! Be steadfast witnesses for Allah in equity, and let not hatred of any people seduce you that ye deal not justly. Deal justly, that is nearer to your duty. Observe your duty to Allah. Lo! Allah is Informed of what ye do

4:48.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَغۡفِرُ أَن يُشۡرَكَ بِهِۦ وَيَغۡفِرُ مَا دُونَ ذَٰلِكَ لِمَن يَشَآءُۚ وَمَن يُشۡرِكۡ بِٱللَّهِ فَقَدِ ٱفۡتَرَىٰٓ إِثۡمًا عَظِيمًا
4:48.en: Lo! Allah forgiveth not that a partner should be ascribed unto Him. He forgiveth (all) save that to whom He will. Whoso ascribeth partners to Allah, he hath indeed invented a tremendous sin

hHblUy44LJw.title: Ramadan 2024 Night 5: Quranic Reflections on Surat An-Nisa
hHblUy44LJw.one_line: An-Nisa as the surah of core values: defending the oppressed, commands that serve us, justice without exceptions, and every nation's prophet.
hHblUy44LJw.summary: He frames An-Nisa as the surah that lays down the value system of Islam before the legal detail of Al-Ma'idah. Its rulings on gender, the vulnerable and the oppressed are moral rulings that a person with sound values would reach unaided, built on three core values: righteousness, justice and incorruptibility. From 4:75 he argues that the stated purpose of armed struggle is to free the oppressed, only ever under a state and its army, and from 4:97-99 that those able to lift oppression carry the blame for those left helpless. The ummah cannot do that today, so he calls for a generation that raises its children for the cause, even if the fruit comes after them, as it did after the Prophet. From 4:66 he notes that Allah only commands what benefits us and still we resist, so children must not experience Islam as a list of prohibitions. He compares the wording of 4:135 with 5:8 and presses the hard case of testifying against a parent or child: a value with an exception is not a value. Finally 4:164 gives the universal lens for dawah: every people had a prophet, and Islam offers them the original form of that message.

outline.heading: The first eight surahs as one cluster
outline.gist: The opening surahs tell the story of how Islam functions: identity, method, protection, then values; An-Nisa supplies the values.

outline.heading: Why Muslims in the West must know their values
outline.gist: A minority's values are combed through by others, so Muslims need to understand the ethics behind their rulings.

outline.heading: Moral-based rulings versus law-based rulings
outline.gist: An-Nisa's rulings, such as those on gender relations, flow from values a person could reach alone, unlike the legal rulings of Al-Ma'idah.

outline.heading: Why lapsed families still hold on to moral rulings
outline.gist: People drop law-based practices first and cling to value-based ones, which shows that humans sense the difference.

outline.heading: Righteousness, justice and incorruptibility
outline.gist: The surah's core values and their opposites; they must be lived before any other part of Islam is preached.

outline.heading: Al-Ma'idah as the contract to sign
outline.gist: After identity, method and values, Al-Ma'idah lists the covenants one by one like the terms of a contract.

outline.heading: Interlude
Companions reluctant to bear arms in Madinah
outline.gist: After thirteen peaceful years in Makkah many companions disliked fighting, and the Quran works to convince them when it is needed.

outline.heading: The cry of the oppressed as the reason to fight
outline.gist: The verse quotes oppressed men, women and children begging for a protector, so the stated purpose of combat is to defend them.

outline.heading: Only within a state and its army
outline.gist: No Muslim civilian may take up arms on his own; the command applies to Muslims with a country and an army.

outline.heading: A value-based reason, not a legal ruling
outline.gist: Defending the oppressed is something one's ethics demand without needing a ruling, tying back to the surah's value of justice.

outline.heading: Those who stayed under oppression and lost their faith
outline.gist: People who died in disbelief blaming oppression are asked why they did not leave; the truly weak with no way out are excused.

outline.heading: Who carries the blame for the helpless
outline.gist: Those who could have defended the oppressed and freed them to choose are the ones held accountable.

outline.heading: A generation that turns the ummah around
outline.gist: The ummah is helpless now but can change if one or two generations understand the deen and raise their children for the cause.

outline.heading: You need not live to see the fruit
outline.gist: The Prophet died before Islam reached three continents; what matters is believing your work is right.

outline.heading: Hard to obey a command you cannot see the light in
outline.gist: Had Allah ordered people to kill themselves or leave their homes few would comply; children likewise obey what they understand.

outline.heading: Every command is in your interest
outline.gist: Allah never commands what harms us, and following the good encouraged would have strengthened people's faith.

outline.heading: Ibrahim and the command with no visible benefit
outline.gist: The order to sacrifice his son was the real test because no benefit could be seen, which is why Eid commemorates it.

outline.heading: Commanded only good and still not listening
outline.gist: Allah could have demanded things against our interest, yet we resist even commands that help us.

outline.heading: Students who thought everything is haram
outline.gist: In his surveys most grade seven and eight students answered that everything is haram; Islam must not be presented as an endless list of no's.

outline.heading: A verse of justice at the United Nations
outline.gist: 4:135 is displayed at the UN headquarters as one of the strongest statements of justice in any scripture.

outline.heading: Why 4:135 and 5:8 switch their wording
outline.gist: An-Nisa leads with standing for justice as an ethic, Al-Ma'idah leads with testimony as a practice, matching each surah's focus.

outline.heading: Testifying against a parent or child
outline.gist: He poses a hit-and-run committed by a loved one: hesitation to testify shows the value of justice is not yet understood.

outline.heading: Rich or poor, do not follow your desire
outline.gist: Whether the party is rich or poor, Allah will deal with them; turning away from justice is known to Him.

outline.heading: A value with an exception is not a value
outline.gist: Justice, generosity and every other ethic must be held across the board; selective values are only a front.

outline.heading: Follow it before being proud of it
outline.gist: Pride in the faith's teaching means nothing unless the value becomes part of who you are.

outline.heading: Prophets we told you of and prophets we did not
outline.gist: The verse gives Muslims a universal lens; a convert loses nothing and can honour where his people came from.

outline.heading: Same theology, different rulings
outline.gist: Earlier prophets brought the same values and belief, while details such as fasting and dietary law differed.

outline.heading: How the hand of man corrupts religion
outline.gist: Many gods, ambiguity and division are profitable and give clergy control, which is why original messages were altered.

outline.heading: Islam is not built to be profitable
outline.gist: Imams are meant to work for a living; a faith that yields wealth and authority is corrupt by nature.

outline.heading: Shared motifs across world religions
outline.gist: Reward, punishment, resurrection, a serpent and a fruit appear from South America to Japan, pointing to one source.

outline.heading: Presenting Islam as the origin of their faith
outline.gist: Allah spoke to Musa and sent prophets we do not know, so Muslims tell others their faith was true in its origin.

outline.heading: Outro

2:255.ar: ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلۡحَيُّ ٱلۡقَيُّومُۚ لَا تَأۡخُذُهُۥ سِنَةࣱ وَلَا نَوۡمࣱۚ لَّهُۥ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۗ مَن ذَا ٱلَّذِي يَشۡفَعُ عِندَهُۥٓ إِلَّا بِإِذۡنِهِۦۚ يَعۡلَمُ مَا بَيۡنَ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَمَا خَلۡفَهُمۡۖ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيۡءࣲ مِّنۡ عِلۡمِهِۦٓ إِلَّا بِمَا شَآءَۚ وَسِعَ كُرۡسِيُّهُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَۖ وَلَا يَـُٔودُهُۥ حِفۡظُهُمَاۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَلِيُّ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ
2:255.en: Allah! There is no deity save Him, the Alive, the Eternal. Neither slumber nor sleep overtaketh Him. Unto Him belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth. Who is he that intercedeth with Him save by His leave? He knoweth that which is in front of them and that which is behind them, while they encompass nothing of His knowledge save what He will. His throne includeth the heavens and the earth, and He is never weary of preserving them. He is the Sublime, the Tremendous

3:2.ar: ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلۡحَيُّ ٱلۡقَيُّومُ
3:2.en: Allah! There is no god save Him, the Alive, the Eternal

20:111.ar: ۞وَعَنَتِ ٱلۡوُجُوهُ لِلۡحَيِّ ٱلۡقَيُّومِۖ وَقَدۡ خَابَ مَنۡ حَمَلَ ظُلۡمࣰ ا

25:58.ar: وَتَوَكَّلۡ عَلَى ٱلۡحَيِّ ٱلَّذِي لَا يَمُوتُ وَسَبِّحۡ بِحَمۡدِهِۦۚ وَكَفَىٰ بِهِۦ بِذُنُوبِ عِبَادِهِۦ خَبِيرًا

40:65.ar: هُوَ ٱلۡحَيُّ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ فَٱدۡعُوهُ مُخۡلِصِينَ لَهُ ٱلدِّينَۗ ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ

57:16.en: Is not the time ripe for the hearts of those who believe to submit to Allah's reminder and to the truth which is revealed, that they become not as those who received the scripture of old but the term was prolonged for them and so their hearts were hardened, and many of them are evil-livers

57:17.ar: ٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحۡيِ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ بَعۡدَ مَوۡتِهَاۚ قَدۡ بَيَّنَّا لَكُمُ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَعۡقِلُونَ

2:260.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ رَبِّ أَرِنِي كَيۡفَ تُحۡيِ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰۖ قَالَ أَوَلَمۡ تُؤۡمِنۖ قَالَ بَلَىٰ وَلَٰكِن لِّيَطۡمَئِنَّ قَلۡبِيۖ قَالَ فَخُذۡ أَرۡبَعَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلطَّيۡرِ فَصُرۡهُنَّ إِلَيۡكَ ثُمَّ ٱجۡعَلۡ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ جَبَلࣲ مِّنۡهُنَّ جُزۡءࣰ ا ثُمَّ ٱدۡعُهُنَّ يَأۡتِينَكَ سَعۡيࣰ اۚ وَٱعۡلَمۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏

8:24.en: O ye who believe! Obey Allah, and the messenger when He calleth you to that which quickeneth you, and know that Allah cometh in between the man and his own heart, and that He it is unto Whom ye will be gathered

36:70.ar: لِّيُنذِرَ مَن كَانَ حَيࣰّ ا وَيَحِقَّ ٱلۡقَوۡلُ عَلَى ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
36:70.en: To warn whosoever liveth, and that the word may be fulfilled against the disbelievers

29:64.ar: وَمَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَآ إِلَّا لَهۡوࣱ وَلَعِبࣱۚ وَإِنَّ ٱلدَّارَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةَ لَهِيَ ٱلۡحَيَوَانُۚ لَوۡ كَانُواْ يَعۡلَمُونَ
29:64.en: This life of the world is but a pastime and a game. Lo! the home of the Hereafter - that is Life, if they but knew

87:13.ar: ثُمَّ لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا وَلَا يَحۡيَىٰ
87:13.en: Wherein he will neither die nor live

HjYH-NivTuw.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: Al-Hayy Al-Qayyum (The Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining)
HjYH-NivTuw.one_line: Al-Hayy and Al-Qayyum: life as the greatest blessing, the life of the spirit, the Hereafter as true life, and haya as heightened sensitivity.
HjYH-NivTuw.summary: Opening the category of names of presence, he pairs Al-Hayy and Al-Qayyum, since the second never appears without the first. Humans neither give themselves life nor sustain it; only Allah is self-subsisting, and some scholars consider this pairing the greatest name. He walks through Ayat al-Kursi and the Prophet's praise of Ubayy for identifying it, and the prophetic duas and istighfar that include these names. Life, he argues, is the ultimate blessing, followed by guidance, and disbelief at its root is covering up that blessing. We once did not exist and everything will perish except Allah. The Quran's main concern, however, is the life of the spirit: a person can breathe and still be dead inside, while Allah revives hearts as He revives dead earth, as shown in Ibrahim's request to see resurrection. True, complete life is the Hereafter. He closes by deriving haya from the same root: not merely modesty but the highest degree of being alive, a heightened sensitivity to how one affects people and to Allah's observation. He asks people to give life figuratively, through medicine, wealth and support, and to cultivate haya.

outline.heading: Two names together; the names of presence
outline.gist: Al-Qayyum only appears paired with Al-Hayy, so he treats them together as the start of the category of names that show Allah's presence.

outline.heading: Al-Qayyum: only Allah sustains Himself
outline.gist: We neither grant nor sustain our own lives; Allah alone is self-subsisting, and some scholars hold this to be the greatest name.

outline.heading: Ayat al-Kursi and Ubayy's answer
outline.gist: The greatest verse describes Allah unlike any other; the Prophet congratulated Ubayy on his knowledge, and Taha also pairs faces humbled before the Ever-Living.

outline.heading: Calling on the Ever-Living in dua
outline.gist: Rely on the Living who never dies; istighfar that includes these names wipes out sins, and the Prophet's dua of submission ends with Allah as the Living who never dies.

outline.heading: Life as the ultimate blessing; kufr as covering it
outline.gist: Life is the greatest blessing, then guidance; kufr means covering a blessing, and denying the blessing of life itself becomes disbelief in Allah.

outline.heading: A time when man was nothing
outline.gist: There was a period when the word human referred to nothing at all, showing that our existence was not always given.

outline.heading: Everything perishes but Him
outline.gist: Every soul tastes death and all on earth perishes except the face of Allah; the false gods are lifeless and do not know when they will be raised.

outline.heading: The dead given life and light
outline.gist: Life in the Quran mainly means the life of the soul; biology is shared with single cells, and this life is a single chance to reach the next level.

outline.heading: Reviving dead hearts like dead earth
outline.gist: Right after asking whether hearts should humble themselves, Allah reminds that He revives dead earth, and so revives dead hearts; the cycle of death and life sustains the world.

outline.heading: Ibrahim asks to see resurrection
outline.gist: Ibrahim's question was about how, not whether; the birds returning to him show Allah brings life from death.

outline.heading: Levels of being alive
outline.gist: Respond to what gives you life; some people breathe yet are not truly living, and starving the spirit kills it like starving the body.

outline.heading: A life with purpose
outline.gist: The higher level of life is knowing Allah and having meaning; a purposeful person uses and values time very differently.

outline.heading: The Hereafter is true life
outline.gist: The Quran calls the Hereafter al-hayawan, the intensified, complete form of life; here we get only the basic version.

outline.heading: Neither dying nor living in Hell
outline.gist: The people of the Fire neither die nor have a life worth living.

outline.heading: Haya: the core ethic of Islam
outline.gist: The Prophet named haya as Islam's core ethic; linguistically it is the pinnacle derived from the root of life.

outline.heading: Haya as heightened sensitivity
outline.gist: Being alive means sensing and responding; haya is the highest sensitivity to how one presents oneself and affects others, from which the meaning of modesty comes.

outline.heading: Haya as a branch of faith
outline.gist: Among the many branches of iman the Prophet singled out haya, sensitivity to people and to Allah's watching.

outline.heading: Living the name: grant life
outline.gist: Give life figuratively, as a physician or through wealth and support that help people actually live.

outline.heading: Living the name: practise haya
outline.gist: Haya is the fullest use of being alive.

themes.label: Spirituality, khushoo and the inner life
themes.note: Real life in the Quran is the life of the spirit; a heart can die while the body functions, and Allah revives it.

W_371Yot7mo.title: Three More Ramadan Reminders
W_371Yot7mo.one_line: From 8:27 on betraying Allah's trust: renew your intention, defy the predictable Ramadan attendance drop, and let hunger answer the call to act for Gaza.
W_371Yot7mo.summary: He opens with 8:27, addressed to believers rather than to those who have merely submitted: do not betray Allah, His Prophet or your trusts. The greatest trust is the Quran and the Prophet's legacy, a baton handed over when the Prophet led all prophets in prayer at al-Aqsa, after which he sought to leave Makkah to carry the message to every nation. Every Muslim carries a piece of it and chooses how much. His first reminder is to renew your intention, since intentions rust; Friday is a checkpoint to review your schedule, time and sleep, with the intention of not being among those who betray. Second, he describes the predictable Ramadan attendance graph he has watched for 30 years, now the worst in 25, perhaps because people relied on his count of 6,500. Fatigue for Allah's sake is rewarded, freedom from the Fire is earned by effort, the Prophet lived only nine Ramadans, and another Ramadan can raise a person above a martyr. Third, drawing on 9:38 about clinging to the earth, he says the hunger of fasting, shared by Gaza, is a call to rise. He asks the young to decide who they are, condemns Canada for halting arms only after 31,000 deaths, and says the decision to change is a private one made in the heart.

outline.heading: Opening
Addressed to believers, not those who merely submitted
outline.gist: 8:27 calls on believers, in whom faith has settled, a level above the Bedouins who were told they had only submitted (49:14). Do not betray Allah and His Prophet.

outline.heading: An amanah is anything entrusted
outline.gist: Allah repeats the warning: do not betray your trusts. A trust can be information, a covenant you agreed to, or a cause you signed on to live for.

outline.heading: The greatest trust: the Book and the Prophet's legacy
outline.gist: We betray Allah and His Prophet when, with the Prophet gone, we throw the Quran and his way behind our backs. Not everyone on earth has access to knowing him; we do.

outline.heading: The baton handed over at al-Aqsa
outline.gist: The Isra could have begun anywhere, but Allah had him lead the spirits of all the prophets in prayer at al-Aqsa: a sign that he and his ummah now carry their message to the end of time.

outline.heading: Seeking a base to reach every nation
outline.gist: Right after the Isra he looked for a tribe to take him out of Makkah. Every nation on earth is the nation of a prophet, and he took on reaching all of them, which needed a base of strength.

outline.heading: Every Muslim carries a piece of the baton
outline.gist: The message spread within a decade of his death and is now carried by all of us equally; each person chooses how much of the burden to take on.

outline.heading: Care for yourself only after full effort (5:105)
outline.gist: We cannot act as if religion is only about ourselves. A khutbah on 5:105 warned against misreading it: look after yourself and stop worrying about those who refuse only once you have done everything you can.

outline.heading: Reminder one: Friday as a checkpoint
outline.gist: Friday in Ramadan is a milestone to hit the brakes: review the schedule you built, your empty time, your sleep, and whether you are actually fasting and praying.

outline.heading: Intentions rust
outline.gist: Ask why you push through hunger, thirst and fatigue. Forgetting is a human advantage that becomes a weakness when we stop reminding ourselves of what matters.

outline.heading: An intention not to betray
outline.gist: A good intention for this Ramadan: I do not want to be among those who threw Your Book and Your Prophet's legacy behind their backs.

outline.heading: Interlude
Reminder two: the predictable Ramadan graph
outline.gist: After about 30 years he knows the curve: a peak, a dip, a slow slide to the 21st night, then spikes. Last year it was broken; this year it is the worst in 25 years.

outline.heading: Everyone counted on someone else
outline.gist: After he shared the 6,500 figure, people assumed others would fill the masjids, like a potluck where everyone brings water. He knows people are tired from work and school.

outline.heading: Beautified fatigue
outline.gist: Every part of your tiredness comes from obeying Allah, so it is banked even while you rest. Bring your best effort, since this may be your last Ramadan.

outline.heading: The parade of Hell
outline.gist: Nothing is worse than Hell. Even before entering it, standing as it is brought forth on 70,000 reins, each held by 70,000 angels, would bring you to your knees.

outline.heading: Freedom by merit, not a lottery
outline.gist: Allah offers to remove those chains, but by merit. Make private dua for the ummah, your heart and repentance; none of us knows how long we have, and the Prophet lived only nine Ramadans.

outline.heading: One more Ramadan above a martyr
outline.gist: Of two men, the one who died a martyr was outranked by the ordinary one who lived another year and fasted another Ramadan. Wasting the season shows ingratitude.

outline.heading: Break the graph
outline.gist: Do not be predictable: when fatigue peaks in a few days, do not skip the night prayer for an in-laws' feast. It is thirty days; focus on worship.

outline.heading: Interlude
What going forth means (9:38)
outline.gist: Why do you cling to the earth when called to go forth? The word means dropping what is in your hand because the call matters more. In Canada that means responsibility and ownership, never violence.

outline.heading: Reminder three: let the hunger call you
outline.gist: Feel your hunger and remember people who have nothing to eat even after sunset. Make this Ramadan a turning point and vow never to return to who you were.

outline.heading: Why are you so heavy?
outline.gist: The verse pictures believers stuck to the ground, content with the small change the world throws at them. Get up, work hard and dedicate yourself.

outline.heading: Young people: decide who you are
outline.gist: Forget the CV: how would you present yourself to Allah? Do you have direction and a life story worth telling, or are you floating aimlessly? Muslims never lived that way.

outline.heading: A rough few centuries, but we can turn it around
outline.gist: The last three or four hundred years have been hard, yet the Quran, the Prophet's light, the masjids and a youthful community remain. Do it for the 31,000 killed for being Muslim and staying on their land.

outline.heading: A government that woke up after 31,000
outline.gist: He is disgusted that Canada halted arms only now, and ashamed that Muslims had too little influence to make their government protect starving women and children.

outline.heading: Allah calls through tragedy
outline.gist: We are still counting the dead because too few decided to live for a different purpose. Allah calls His people through hardship like this, while most prefer to wait passively for it to end.

outline.heading: A decision made in the heart
outline.gist: This is a wake-up call. The decision is personal and unseen except by the One calling you: make this month a turning point and ask Him to make you who you want to be.

outline.heading: Outro

14:12.ar: وَمَا لَنَآ أَلَّا نَتَوَكَّلَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ وَقَدۡ هَدَىٰنَا سُبُلَنَاۚ وَلَنَصۡبِرَنَّ عَلَىٰ مَآ ءَاذَيۡتُمُونَاۚ وَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَلۡيَتَوَكَّلِ ٱلۡمُتَوَكِّلُونَ
14:12.en: How should we not put our trust in Allah when He hath shown us our ways? We surely will endure the hurt ye do us. In Allah let the trusting put their trust

14:42.ar: وَلَا تَحۡسَبَنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَٰفِلًا عَمَّا يَعۡمَلُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَۚ إِنَّمَا يُؤَخِّرُهُمۡ لِيَوۡمࣲ تَشۡخَصُ فِيهِ ٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرُ
14:42.en: Deem not that Allah is unaware of what the wicked do. He but giveth them a respite till a day when eyes will stare (in terror)

14:43.ar: مُهۡطِعِينَ مُقۡنِعِي رُءُوسِهِمۡ لَا يَرۡتَدُّ إِلَيۡهِمۡ طَرۡفُهُمۡۖ وَأَفۡـِٔدَتُهُمۡ هَوَآءࣱ‏
14:43.en: As they come hurrying on in fear, their heads upraised, their gaze returning not to them, and their hearts as air

15:14.ar: وَلَوۡ فَتَحۡنَا عَلَيۡهِم بَابࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَظَلُّواْ فِيهِ يَعۡرُجُونَ
15:14.en: And even if We opened unto them a gate of heaven and they kept mounting through it

15:15.ar: لَقَالُوٓاْ إِنَّمَا سُكِّرَتۡ أَبۡصَٰرُنَا بَلۡ نَحۡنُ قَوۡمࣱ مَّسۡحُورُونَ
15:15.en: They would say: Our sight is wrong - nay, but we are folk bewitched

15:53.ar: قَالُواْ لَا تَوۡجَلۡ إِنَّا نُبَشِّرُكَ بِغُلَٰمٍ عَلِيمࣲ‏
15:53.en: They said: Be not afraid! Lo! we bring thee good tidings of a boy possessing wisdom

15:54.ar: قَالَ أَبَشَّرۡتُمُونِي عَلَىٰٓ أَن مَّسَّنِيَ ٱلۡكِبَرُ فَبِمَ تُبَشِّرُونَ
15:54.en: He said: Bring ye me good tidings (of a son) when old age hath overtaken me? Of what then can ye bring good tidings

15:55.ar: قَالُواْ بَشَّرۡنَٰكَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ فَلَا تَكُن مِّنَ ٱلۡقَٰنِطِينَ
15:55.en: They said: We bring thee good tidings in truth. So be not thou of the despairing

15:56.ar: قَالَ وَمَن يَقۡنَطُ مِن رَّحۡمَةِ رَبِّهِۦٓ إِلَّا ٱلضَّآلُّونَ
15:56.en: He said: And who despaireth of the mercy of his Lord save those who are astray

16:8.ar: وَٱلۡخَيۡلَ وَٱلۡبِغَالَ وَٱلۡحَمِيرَ لِتَرۡكَبُوهَا وَزِينَةࣰۚ وَيَخۡلُقُ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ

16:66.ar: وَإِنَّ لَكُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَنۡعَٰمِ لَعِبۡرَةࣰۖ نُّسۡقِيكُم مِّمَّا فِي بُطُونِهِۦ مِنۢ بَيۡنِ فَرۡثࣲ وَدَمࣲ لَّبَنًا خَالِصࣰ ا سَآئِغࣰ ا لِّلشَّٰرِبِينَ
16:66.en: And lo! in the cattle there is a lesson for you. We give you to drink of that which is in their bellies, from betwixt the refuse and the blood, pure milk palatable to the drinkers

14:34.ar: وَءَاتَىٰكُم مِّن كُلِّ مَا سَأَلۡتُمُوهُۚ وَإِن تَعُدُّواْ نِعۡمَتَ ٱللَّهِ لَا تُحۡصُوهَآۗ إِنَّ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ لَظَلُومࣱ كَفَّارࣱ‏
14:34.en: And He giveth you of all ye ask of Him, and if ye would count the bounty of Allah ye cannot reckon it. Lo! man is verily a wrong-doer, an ingrate

14:35.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِيمُ رَبِّ ٱجۡعَلۡ هَٰذَا ٱلۡبَلَدَ ءَامِنࣰ ا وَٱجۡنُبۡنِي وَبَنِيَّ أَن نَّعۡبُدَ ٱلۡأَصۡنَامَ
14:35.en: And when Abraham said: My Lord! Make safe this territory, and preserve me and my sons from serving idols

14:36.ar: رَبِّ إِنَّهُنَّ أَضۡلَلۡنَ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِۖ فَمَن تَبِعَنِي فَإِنَّهُۥ مِنِّيۖ وَمَنۡ عَصَانِي فَإِنَّكَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
14:36.en: My Lord! Lo! they have led many of mankind astray. But whoso followeth me, he verily is of me. And whoso disobeyeth me - Still Thou art Forgiving, Merciful

14:37.ar: رَّبَّنَآ إِنِّيٓ أَسۡكَنتُ مِن ذُرِّيَّتِي بِوَادٍ غَيۡرِ ذِي زَرۡعٍ عِندَ بَيۡتِكَ ٱلۡمُحَرَّمِ رَبَّنَا لِيُقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ فَٱجۡعَلۡ أَفۡـِٔدَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ تَهۡوِيٓ إِلَيۡهِمۡ وَٱرۡزُقۡهُم مِّنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَشۡكُرُونَ
14:37.en: Our Lord! Lo! I have settled some of my posterity in an uncultivable valley near unto Thy holy House, our Lord! that they may establish proper worship; so incline some hearts of men that they may yearn toward them, and provide Thou them with fruits in order that they may be thankful

14:38.ar: رَبَّنَآ إِنَّكَ تَعۡلَمُ مَا نُخۡفِي وَمَا نُعۡلِنُۗ وَمَا يَخۡفَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ مِن شَيۡءࣲ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَا فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ
14:38.en: Our Lord! Lo! Thou knowest that which we hide and that which we proclaim. Nothing in the earth or in the heaven is hidden from Allah

14:39.ar: ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِي وَهَبَ لِي عَلَى ٱلۡكِبَرِ إِسۡمَٰعِيلَ وَإِسۡحَٰقَۚ إِنَّ رَبِّي لَسَمِيعُ ٱلدُّعَآءِ
14:39.en: Praise be to Allah Who hath given me, in my old age, Ishmael and Isaac! Lo! my Lord is indeed the Hearer of Prayer

14:40.ar: رَبِّ ٱجۡعَلۡنِي مُقِيمَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِيۚ رَبَّنَا وَتَقَبَّلۡ دُعَآءِ
14:40.en: My Lord! Make me to establish proper worship, and some of my posterity (also); our Lord! and accept my prayer

14:41.ar: رَبَّنَا ٱغۡفِرۡ لِي وَلِوَٰلِدَيَّ وَلِلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ يَوۡمَ يَقُومُ ٱلۡحِسَابُ
14:41.en: Our Lord! Forgive me and my parents and believers on the day when the account is cast

15:2.ar: رُّبَمَا يَوَدُّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَوۡ كَانُواْ مُسۡلِمِينَ
15:2.en: It may be that those who disbelieve wish ardently that they were Muslims

15:26.ar: وَلَقَدۡ خَلَقۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ مِن صَلۡصَٰلࣲ مِّنۡ حَمَإࣲ مَّسۡنُونࣲ‏
15:26.en: Verily We created man of potter's clay of black mud altered

15:27.ar: وَٱلۡجَآنَّ خَلَقۡنَٰهُ مِن قَبۡلُ مِن نَّارِ ٱلسَّمُومِ
15:27.en: And the jinn did We create aforetime of essential fire

15:28.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّي خَٰلِقُۢ بَشَرࣰ ا مِّن صَلۡصَٰلࣲ مِّنۡ حَمَإࣲ مَّسۡنُونࣲ‏
15:28.en: And (remember) when thy Lord said unto the angels: Lo! I am creating a mortal out of potter's clay of black mud altered

15:29.ar: فَإِذَا سَوَّيۡتُهُۥ وَنَفَخۡتُ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِي فَقَعُواْ لَهُۥ سَٰجِدِينَ
15:29.en: So, when I have made him and have breathed into him of My Spirit, do ye fall down, prostrating yourselves unto him

15:30.en: So the angels fell prostrate, all of them together

15:31.ar: إِلَّآ إِبۡلِيسَ أَبَىٰٓ أَن يَكُونَ مَعَ ٱلسَّٰجِدِينَ
15:31.en: Save Iblis. He refused to be among the prostrate

15:32.ar: قَالَ يَٰٓإِبۡلِيسُ مَا لَكَ أَلَّا تَكُونَ مَعَ ٱلسَّٰجِدِينَ
15:32.en: He said: O Iblis! What aileth thee that thou art not among the prostrate

15:33.ar: قَالَ لَمۡ أَكُن لِّأَسۡجُدَ لِبَشَرٍ خَلَقۡتَهُۥ مِن صَلۡصَٰلࣲ مِّنۡ حَمَإࣲ مَّسۡنُونࣲ‏
15:33.en: He said: I am not one to prostrate myself unto a mortal whom Thou hast created out of potter's clay of black mud altered

14:7.ar: وَإِذۡ تَأَذَّنَ رَبُّكُمۡ لَئِن شَكَرۡتُمۡ لَأَزِيدَنَّكُمۡۖ وَلَئِن كَفَرۡتُمۡ إِنَّ عَذَابِي لَشَدِيدࣱ‏
14:7.en: And when your Lord proclaimed: If ye give thanks, I will give you more; but if ye are thankless, lo! My punishment is dire

8foOMLW1tYk.title: Ramadan 2024 Night 13: Quranic Reflections on Ibrahim, Al-Hijr and An-Nahl
8foOMLW1tYk.one_line: The cluster of blessings: gratitude for guidance, Allah's awareness of oppressors, learning to see blessings, never despairing, beauty in creation, and purified deeds.
8foOMLW1tYk.summary: He presents Ibrahim, Al-Hijr and An-Nahl as a cluster on blessings: Ibrahim on showing gratitude before blessings are lost, Al-Hijr on the ability to recognise them at all, as Iblis failed to see Adam's potential and Lut's people stopped valuing family, and An-Nahl on seeing every blessing as coming from one source and using it by His rules. From 14:12 he shows that gratitude for guidance means relying on Allah and persevering under persecution, since guidance is a gift, not an achievement. From 14:42-43 he assures the oppressed that no injustice escapes Allah; oppressors are only postponed. He warns that mass brutality, as after the Arab Spring, either raises iman or destroys it. From 15:14-15 he describes people so unable to acknowledge blessings that even soaring through the heavens would not convince them, and urges realism over pessimism. Ibrahim's brief doubt at the news of a son, quickly corrected, shows how to recover hope. From 16:8 he draws out the beauty Allah placed in creation, which youth miss, and from 16:66 he asks that deeds be offered as pure as milk drawn from between blood and waste.

outline.heading: Opening
Hold your standard as Ramadan slips away
outline.gist: As the month speeds up, keep pushing yourself, especially when unsure whether Allah has accepted you.

outline.heading: Interlude
A cluster of surahs on blessings
outline.gist: Ibrahim, Al-Hijr and An-Nahl each look at Allah's blessings from a different angle.

outline.heading: Ibrahim: show gratitude or lose the blessing
outline.gist: Gratitude and good use of blessings keep them from being taken; Ibrahim's late-life duas are full of thanks despite his hardships.

outline.heading: Al-Hijr: the ability to acknowledge blessings
outline.gist: You cannot thank what you do not see as a blessing; entitlement and taking things for granted block gratitude.

outline.heading: Others may wish they had what you have
outline.gist: The surah opens noting disbelievers may wish they were Muslim, a blessing believers often fail to notice.

outline.heading: Iblis could not see Adam's potential
outline.gist: Adam's worth came from the union of earth and spirit; Iblis judged by origin and missed it.

outline.heading: Lut's people stopped seeing the blessing of family
outline.gist: They lost sight of spouses, children and functional families; must Allah take something away before we see it?

outline.heading: An-Nahl: every blessing has one source
outline.gist: Whatever route a blessing takes, it comes from Allah and must be used by His rules; anything becomes provision once seen that way.

outline.heading: Interlude
Every prophet and his doubting people
outline.gist: A generic story: people doubt their prophets and demand signs, and prophets reply that signs come only with Allah's permission.

outline.heading: Why would we not rely on Allah?
outline.gist: Persecuted and threatened with exile, the prophets ask how they could not rely on the One who guided their ways.

outline.heading: Guidance is a blessing to be thanked
outline.gist: Most people invent their answers about life as they go; believers were given authentic answers.

outline.heading: Gratitude for guidance is shown in action
outline.gist: Thanks means relying on Allah and continuing the mission even when losing status and ground.

outline.heading: Persevering through harm
outline.gist: The prophets vow patience under persecution; guidance is not an achievement, and seeing it as a gift sustains perseverance.

outline.heading: Never think Allah is unaware of the oppressors
outline.gist: The emphatic form rules out any thought that Allah overlooks even the smallest act of oppression.

outline.heading: No wrong is ever lost
outline.gist: Even oppression too subtle to explain or prove is seen, as are the massive killings now under way.

outline.heading: Brutality either raises iman or destroys it
outline.gist: Witnessing great bloodshed turns some into people of causes and makes others abandon faith.

outline.heading: The Arab Spring and a shaken ummah
outline.gist: Bloodshed in Egypt, Syria, Libya and Yemen weakened many people's iman because they did not see it as the hard labour of an ummah rising after centuries of decline.

outline.heading: Postponed to a day of staring eyes
outline.gist: Oppressors are delayed to a day they walk dazed like patients after anaesthesia, so trust Allah's justice.

outline.heading: His first reflection at sixteen
outline.gist: This was the first verse he tried to explain publicly, recorded on an old VHS tape.

outline.heading: Neither pessimist nor optimist
outline.gist: A Muslim is a realist who sees what is missing and works for it while acknowledging what is there.

outline.heading: Ascending through a gate in the sky
outline.gist: Even if a gate to the heavens were opened, they would climb on a curved path, a detail he offers as a nugget for scientists.

outline.heading: Our eyes are dazzled, we are bewitched
outline.gist: Shown the whole universe, they would claim a spell or darkness; nothing satisfies them.

outline.heading: Could have been better, could have been worse
outline.gist: There are endless ways things could be better and equally endless ways worse, so acknowledge the good in what you have.

outline.heading: Regret over people taken for granted
outline.gist: Many spend years regretting relationships with parents, siblings and friends whose value they missed until they were gone.

outline.heading: The blessing of an appetite
outline.gist: Patients he works with long for one meal without nausea; simple functions deserve thanks and make you a better person.

outline.heading: Ibrahim's story told in patches
outline.gist: Ibrahim, Isma'il and the Ka'bah, and the line of Isma'il as its caretakers.

outline.heading: Good news of a son at ninety
outline.gist: Angels on their way to Lut's people bring news of a son, and Ibrahim asks what good news this is at his age.

outline.heading: Do not be among the despairing
outline.gist: For a moment even Ibrahim lost sight of the blessing, and the angels told him not to lose hope.

outline.heading: Who despairs of his Lord's mercy?
outline.gist: Ibrahim corrected himself at once: only the misguided despair; a good Muslim quickly returns to seeing the good.

outline.heading: You do not know what will be good for you
outline.gist: From the son he doubted came a long line of prophets; a gift's value may not be visible at first.

outline.heading: Horses, mules and donkeys to ride and to adorn
outline.gist: An-Nahl counts blessing after blessing; these animals are for transport and also for beauty.

outline.heading: The beauty of humble animals
outline.gist: Donkeys and mules are kind, intelligent and beautiful; creation has an artistic side Allah asks us to notice.

outline.heading: Colourblind people seeing colour for the first time
outline.gist: Men in tears staring at the sky remind us how much beauty we ignore every day.

outline.heading: He creates what you do not know
outline.gist: Undiscovered beauty fills the universe, and the Quran itself must be recited with an artistic tune.

outline.heading: Beauty as a way into the Quran
outline.gist: Beyond being logical and beneficial, Allah's teachings are beautiful, and missing that loses part of their meaning.

outline.heading: Why youth do not connect
outline.gist: Young people lack the lens of beauty for the deen, and the community must find ways to help them see it.

outline.heading: Pure milk from between blood and waste
outline.gist: Allah draws pure, pleasant milk out of an animal's belly from between dung and blood.

outline.heading: Offer Allah deeds as pure as that milk
outline.gist: Purify worship of vanity, showing off, the need for recognition, envy and arrogance.

outline.heading: Would you drink milk mixed with filth?
outline.gist: If you would refuse such milk, do not expect Allah to accept a deed mixed with impurity.

themes.note: Guidance is a gift thanked through reliance on Allah and perseverance under persecution.

themes.label: Justice and refusing oppression

themes.label: Eman: faith, certainty, doubt

themes.label: Gratitude (shukr) and appreciation

themes.label: Hope, fear and the balance between them
themes.note: Ibrahim's quick recovery from doubt shows that only the misguided despair of Allah's mercy.

themes.label: Beauty, art and the aesthetic sense in faith
themes.note: Creation and the Quran carry beauty Allah wants us to notice; without that lens the deen is only partly understood.

themes.label: Youth, their challenges and their role
themes.note: Youth disconnect from the deen partly because no one helps them see its beauty.

themes.note: Deeds must be purified of showing off, vanity, envy and arrogance as milk is purified for us.

9:103.ar: خُذۡ مِنۡ أَمۡوَٰلِهِمۡ صَدَقَةࣰ تُطَهِّرُهُمۡ وَتُزَكِّيهِم بِهَا وَصَلِّ عَلَيۡهِمۡۖ إِنَّ صَلَوٰتَكَ سَكَنࣱ لَّهُمۡۗ وَٱللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ
9:103.en: Take alms of their wealth, wherewith thou mayst purify them and mayst make them grow, and pray for them. Lo! thy prayer is an assuagement for them. Allah is Hearer, Knower

9:111.ar: ۞إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱشۡتَرَىٰ مِنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ أَنفُسَهُمۡ وَأَمۡوَٰلَهُم بِأَنَّ لَهُمُ ٱلۡجَنَّةَۚ يُقَٰتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ فَيَقۡتُلُونَ وَيُقۡتَلُونَۖ وَعۡدًا عَلَيۡهِ حَقࣰّ ا فِي ٱلتَّوۡرَىٰةِ وَٱلۡإِنجِيلِ وَٱلۡقُرۡءَانِۚ وَمَنۡ أَوۡفَىٰ بِعَهۡدِهِۦ مِنَ ٱللَّهِۚ فَٱسۡتَبۡشِرُواْ بِبَيۡعِكُمُ ٱلَّذِي بَايَعۡتُم بِهِۦۚ وَذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلۡفَوۡزُ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ
9:111.en: Lo! Allah hath bought from the believers their lives and their wealth because the Garden will be theirs: they shall fight in the way of Allah and shall slay and be slain. It is a promise which is binding on Him in the Torah and the Gospel and the Qur'an. Who fulfilleth His covenant better than Allah? Rejoice then in your bargain that ye have made, for that is the supreme triumph

10:7.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَرۡجُونَ لِقَآءَنَا وَرَضُواْ بِٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَٱطۡمَأَنُّواْ بِهَا وَٱلَّذِينَ هُمۡ عَنۡ ءَايَٰتِنَا غَٰفِلُونَ
10:7.en: Lo! those who expect not the meeting with Us but desire the life of the world and feel secure therein, and those who are neglectful of Our revelations

10:8.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ مَأۡوَىٰهُمُ ٱلنَّارُ بِمَا كَانُواْ يَكۡسِبُونَ
10:8.en: Their home will be the Fire because of what they used to earn

10:22.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي يُسَيِّرُكُمۡ فِي ٱلۡبَرِّ وَٱلۡبَحۡرِۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا كُنتُمۡ فِي ٱلۡفُلۡكِ وَجَرَيۡنَ بِهِم بِرِيحࣲ طَيِّبَةࣲ وَفَرِحُواْ بِهَا جَآءَتۡهَا رِيحٌ عَاصِفࣱ وَجَآءَهُمُ ٱلۡمَوۡجُ مِن كُلِّ مَكَانࣲ وَظَنُّوٓاْ أَنَّهُمۡ أُحِيطَ بِهِمۡ دَعَوُاْ ٱللَّهَ مُخۡلِصِينَ لَهُ ٱلدِّينَ لَئِنۡ أَنجَيۡتَنَا مِنۡ هَٰذِهِۦ لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلشَّٰكِرِينَ
10:22.en: He it is Who maketh you to go on the land and the sea till, when ye are in the ships and they sail with them with a fair breeze and they are glad therein, a storm-wind reacheth them and the wave cometh unto them from every side and they deem that they are overwhelmed therein; (then) they cry unto Allah, making their faith pure for Him only: If Thou deliver us from this, we truly will be of the thankful

10:23.ar: فَلَمَّآ أَنجَىٰهُمۡ إِذَا هُمۡ يَبۡغُونَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ بِغَيۡرِ ٱلۡحَقِّۗ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّمَا بَغۡيُكُمۡ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِكُمۖ مَّتَٰعَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَاۖ ثُمَّ إِلَيۡنَا مَرۡجِعُكُمۡ فَنُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
10:23.en: Yet when He hath delivered them, behold! they rebel in the earth wrongfully. O mankind! Your rebellion is only against yourselves. (Ye have) enjoyment of the life of the world; then unto Us is your return and We shall proclaim unto you what ye used to do

9:118.ar: وَعَلَى ٱلثَّلَٰثَةِ ٱلَّذِينَ خُلِّفُواْ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا ضَاقَتۡ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ بِمَا رَحُبَتۡ وَضَاقَتۡ عَلَيۡهِمۡ أَنفُسُهُمۡ وَظَنُّوٓاْ أَن لَّا مَلۡجَأَ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّآ إِلَيۡهِ ثُمَّ تَابَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ لِيَتُوبُوٓاْۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
9:118.en: And to the three also (did He turn in mercy) who were left behind, when the earth, vast as it is, was straitened for them, and their own souls were straitened for them till they bethought them that there is no refuge from Allah save toward Him. Then turned He unto them in mercy that they (too) might turn (repentant unto Him). Lo! Allah! He is the Relenting, the Merciful

kG577e5dhTo.title: Ramadan 2024 Night 10: Quranic Reflections on At-Tawbah and Yunus
kG577e5dhTo.one_line: Reading At-Tawbah in context, the untrained soul's cycle of vanity and pleading, the sale of self to Allah, charity as proof of honesty, and investing in the hereafter.
kG577e5dhTo.summary: He opens by insisting At-Tawbah must be read in its context: a Muslim-majority state facing tribes that broke their treaties some 27 times, which explains its firmness; lifting its commands literally into different settings creates extremists, as copying the Prophet's outward actions without their purpose does. He outlines the Tabuk campaign and introduces the next cluster of surahs, noting that in Yunus haqq means purposefulness against aimlessness. From 10:22-23 he describes the untrained soul's cycle: vain in good times, pleading in a storm, forgetting once rescued; believers must keep the humility of their lowest moment. From 9:111 he presents all of Islam as a contract in which Allah buys our selves and possessions for Paradise; war is hated and rarely required, and most people fulfil the contract through their own profession. From 9:103 he explains sadaqah as a testament of honesty, warns against holding wealth owed to others, and rebukes a community that has grown stingy toward the institutions that advocate for and support it. From 10:7-8 and the Prophet's distribution of a sheep he urges people to build their hereafter, since only what is given away remains.

outline.heading: Opening
At-Tawbah organises relations with non-Muslims
outline.gist: It addresses those who fight and those who do not, foreign powers and those living among Muslims, a theme revisited briefly in the twenty-eighth juz.

outline.heading: The context of a Muslim-majority state
outline.gist: The surah assumes Muslims govern a nation by Allah's word; ignoring that produces extremists who contradict the Quran.

outline.heading: Literal reading needs the same circumstances
outline.gist: Commands are followed literally only in the same setting; otherwise follow the purpose behind them, as with the Prophet's actions, or the outward copy misses the objective.

outline.heading: A dare to explain At-Tawbah
outline.gist: Someone once challenged him to teach the surah; it is easy with context, and the surah of repentance is full of mercy.

outline.heading: Treaties broken again and again
outline.gist: Neighbouring tribes signed treaties and then murdered Muslims; the Prophet renewed them some 27 times before the Quran ended it with a four-month ultimatum.

outline.heading: Context makes the verses make sense
outline.gist: Someone who keeps breaking trust cannot keep being offered new contracts; without that context the verses are misread.

outline.heading: Why the Prophet marched to Tabuk
outline.gist: Arab allies of the Romans kept plotting to wipe out Madinah; when the Prophet arrived they fled.

outline.heading: The hardship of Tabuk and those who stayed behind
outline.gist: A thousand kilometres in summer heat during poverty; hypocrites lied to excuse themselves, and three believers stayed back with no excuse.

outline.heading: The second cluster and the four disciplines of faith
outline.gist: Yunus to Ar-Ra'd each address a critical point in theology, the message, values or law; Yunus addresses theology and decree.

outline.heading: Haqq as purposefulness
outline.gist: In Yunus haqq contrasts with aimlessness, not falsehood: the universe was created with purpose.

outline.heading: Fair winds, then the storm
outline.gist: Sailors enjoying good winds are struck by a storm, feel surrounded, and call on Allah sincerely, promising gratitude.

outline.heading: Rescued, they return to arrogance
outline.gist: Once safe on land they go back to vanity and oppression on earth.

outline.heading: Your oppression harms only you
outline.gist: Allah warns that their transgression rebounds on them; much of life simply happens to us and we must respond.

outline.heading: The cycle of the untrained soul
outline.gist: In ease it takes credit and grows vain; in hardship it turns to Allah broken and humble; then it forgets.

outline.heading: We all forget our promises
outline.gist: People ask for one thing, swear they will want nothing more, then go back to wanting more once it is granted.

outline.heading: Keep the humility of your lowest moment
outline.gist: Like a prisoner who swore never to complain once freed, the soul's disloyalty must be kept in check.

outline.heading: Striving in the context of external threats
outline.gist: The verse concerns striving in general, though its setting includes combat against enemies at Tabuk.

outline.heading: No one sane wants war
outline.gist: War ruins minds for generations; the trauma of the Second World War is still carried today.

outline.heading: Muslims had to be pushed to defend themselves
outline.gist: Failing to defend rights would bring worse harm; the idea that Muslims are bloodthirsty ignores what the Quran says.

outline.heading: There was no battle at Tabuk
outline.gist: The opposing armies quarrelled and dispersed; the Muslims camped three nights and returned without a fight.

outline.heading: Allah has bought their selves and wealth
outline.gist: What comes from Allah is a blessing; once in your hands it is mal, which includes status and degrees as well as money.

outline.heading: All of Islam as one contract
outline.gist: Give yourself and what you own; in return Allah gives Paradise.

outline.heading: Many fields of striving
outline.gist: The promise is in the Torah, Injil and Quran; striving may be knowledge, advocacy, outreach or finance, and historically under one percent died in combat.

outline.heading: Why combat is singled out
outline.gist: When life is on the line sincerity is exposed, which is why the Quran speaks of it.

outline.heading: The best deal ever made
outline.gist: You give up what was never yours and is temporary for something permanent and beyond any comparable value.

outline.heading: Every profession signs differently
outline.gist: Physicians, lawyers, engineers, teachers and workers each offer what they have where they are.

outline.heading: Sadaqah as a testament of honesty
outline.gist: The word comes from truthfulness: giving hard-earned money proves you take the faith seriously.

outline.heading: Even a smile proves your honesty
outline.gist: Smiling when tired is not charity but proof of adherence to what Allah asked.

outline.heading: Purifying wealth of what belongs to others
outline.gist: No money with someone else's name on it should sit in your hands; the longer it stays the harder it is to release.

outline.heading: Rights in wealth beyond zakah
outline.gist: Family, parents and the needy have claims on your wealth; when people are starving, giving becomes obligatory, not optional.

outline.heading: Giving from what you still need
outline.gist: The Prophet's prayer brings calm because giving is hard; Islam expects giving even from money you wish to keep, beyond basic needs.

outline.heading: Companions who brought everything
outline.gist: Some brought all they owned and were told to keep half; he does not ask people to bankrupt themselves.

outline.heading: A community that stopped giving
outline.gist: Compared with a decade ago people hold on to wealth while advocacy and support organisations cannot pay their staff.

outline.heading: Who owes whom
outline.gist: The giver is the one who gains; withholding what is owed to others is the worst burden after shedding blood.

outline.heading: Content with this life, not hoping to meet Allah
outline.gist: Those who do not expect to meet Allah are satisfied with worldly life and settle into it.

outline.heading: The caliph and Abu Hazim
outline.gist: On Hajj an Umayyad caliph asked for someone who had met the companions, and the elderly Abu Hazim made him come to him.

outline.heading: Why we love this life and dread the next
outline.gist: Asked in tears, Abu Hazim answered that they built their worldly life and left their hereafter a ruin.

outline.heading: Are you looking forward to what Allah promised
outline.gist: If the focus is only how much one can build and have, the hereafter becomes something to dread.

outline.heading: The heedless and their investment
outline.gist: Those indifferent to Allah's teaching end in the Fire; do not throw pennies at the hereafter while investing everything now.

outline.heading: All of it remains except the shoulder
outline.gist: The Prophet gave away a slaughtered sheep piece by piece and said what was given remains, while what is eaten is gone.

themes.label: Methodology: how to read texts, tafsir method, intellectual approach
themes.note: Verses and prophetic actions must be read in their context; literalism in a different setting misses the purpose.

themes.label: Extremism, bad religiosity and distorted practice
themes.note: Projecting At-Tawbah onto minority or non-Islamic contexts produces extremist behaviour.

themes.label: Seerah events and their lessons
themes.note: Repeated treaty betrayals and the Tabuk campaign explain At-Tawbah's tone.

themes.label: Tazkiyah: purifying and training the self
themes.note: The untrained soul swings between vanity and pleading and forgets; it must be trained to keep its humility.

themes.label: Mujahadah: striving as a way of life
themes.note: Allah has bought the believers' selves and possessions; each person strives in his own field, and combat is rare and never desired.

themes.label: Zakat, charity and giving
themes.note: Charity proves honesty, purifies wealth and soul, and is due beyond zakah when people are in need.

themes.label: Community building, cooperation and the ummah
themes.note: Local advocacy and support institutions are failing for lack of community funding.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: People dread the hereafter because they built only this world; what is given away is what remains.

stories.point: The surah is easy to explain once its context is known.

stories.who: Treaties renewed some 27 times
stories.point: The Prophet kept forgiving betrayals for peace until the Quran ruled that repeated treachery ends the relationship.

stories.who: The Tabuk campaign
stories.point: A costly march in heat and poverty that ended with no battle because the enemy dispersed.

stories.who: The three who stayed behind from Tabuk
stories.point: Believers who stayed back without excuse, unlike hypocrites who lied.
