takeaways: Read At-Tawbah and every command in its context, following its purpose when circumstances differ
When relief comes, keep the humility and gratitude you had in your hardest moment
See your life and possessions as already sold to Allah and serve Him through your own profession
Give even from wealth you would like to keep, clear any money owed to others, and fund the institutions that advocate for and support the community
Invest in the hereafter by giving, since only what you give away remains

11:61.ar: ۞وَإِلَىٰ ثَمُودَ أَخَاهُمۡ صَٰلِحࣰ اۚ قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ ٱعۡبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنۡ إِلَٰهٍ غَيۡرُهُۥۖ هُوَ أَنشَأَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱسۡتَعۡمَرَكُمۡ فِيهَا فَٱسۡتَغۡفِرُوهُ ثُمَّ تُوبُوٓاْ إِلَيۡهِۚ إِنَّ رَبِّي قَرِيبࣱ مُّجِيبࣱ‏
11:61.en: And unto (the tribe of) Thamud (We sent) their brother Salih. He said: O my people! Serve Allah, Ye have no other Allah save Him. He brought you forth from the earth and hath made you husband it. So ask forgiveness of Him and turn unto Him repentant. Lo! my Lord is Nigh, Responsive

37:75.en: And Noah verily prayed unto Us, and gracious was the Hearer of his prayer

2:186.ar: وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِي عَنِّي فَإِنِّي قَرِيبٌۖ أُجِيبُ دَعۡوَةَ ٱلدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِۖ فَلۡيَسۡتَجِيبُواْ لِي وَلۡيُؤۡمِنُواْ بِي لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَرۡشُدُونَ
2:186.en: And when My servants question thee concerning Me, then surely I am nigh. I answer the prayer of the suppliant when he crieth unto Me. So let them hear My call and let them trust in Me, in order that they may be led aright

21:84.ar: فَٱسۡتَجَبۡنَا لَهُۥ فَكَشَفۡنَا مَا بِهِۦ مِن ضُرࣲّۖ وَءَاتَيۡنَٰهُ أَهۡلَهُۥ وَمِثۡلَهُم مَّعَهُمۡ رَحۡمَةࣰ مِّنۡ عِندِنَا وَذِكۡرَىٰ لِلۡعَٰبِدِينَ
21:84.en: Then We heard his prayer and removed that adversity from which he suffered, and We gave him his household (that he had lost) and the like thereof along with them, a mercy from Our store, and a remembrance for the worshippers

21:76.ar: وَنُوحًا إِذۡ نَادَىٰ مِن قَبۡلُ فَٱسۡتَجَبۡنَا لَهُۥ فَنَجَّيۡنَٰهُ وَأَهۡلَهُۥ مِنَ ٱلۡكَرۡبِ ٱلۡعَظِيمِ
21:76.en: And Noah, when he cried of old, We heard his prayer and saved him and his household from the great affliction

21:88.ar: فَٱسۡتَجَبۡنَا لَهُۥ وَنَجَّيۡنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلۡغَمِّۚ وَكَذَٰلِكَ نُـۨجِي ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
21:88.en: Then we heard his prayer and saved him from the anguish. Thus we save believers

21:90.ar: فَٱسۡتَجَبۡنَا لَهُۥ وَوَهَبۡنَا لَهُۥ يَحۡيَىٰ وَأَصۡلَحۡنَا لَهُۥ زَوۡجَهُۥٓۚ إِنَّهُمۡ كَانُواْ يُسَٰرِعُونَ فِي ٱلۡخَيۡرَٰتِ وَيَدۡعُونَنَا رَغَبࣰ ا وَرَهَبࣰ اۖ وَكَانُواْ لَنَا خَٰشِعِينَ
21:90.en: Then We heard his prayer, and bestowed upon him John, and adjusted his wife (to bear a child) for him. Lo! they used to vie one with the other in good deeds, and they cried unto Us in longing and in fear, and were submissive unto Us

3:195.ar: فَٱسۡتَجَابَ لَهُمۡ رَبُّهُمۡ أَنِّي لَآ أُضِيعُ عَمَلَ عَٰمِلࣲ مِّنكُم مِّن ذَكَرٍ أَوۡ أُنثَىٰۖ بَعۡضُكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡضࣲۖ فَٱلَّذِينَ هَاجَرُواْ وَأُخۡرِجُواْ مِن دِيَٰرِهِمۡ وَأُوذُواْ فِي سَبِيلِي وَقَٰتَلُواْ وَقُتِلُواْ لَأُكَفِّرَنَّ عَنۡهُمۡ سَيِّـَٔاتِهِمۡ وَلَأُدۡخِلَنَّهُمۡ جَنَّٰتࣲ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ ثَوَابࣰ ا مِّنۡ عِندِ ٱللَّهِۚ وَٱللَّهُ عِندَهُۥ حُسۡنُ ٱلثَّوَابِ
3:195.en: And their Lord hath heard them (and He saith): Lo! I suffer not the work of any worker, male or female, to be lost. Ye proceed one from another. So those who fled and were driven forth from their homes and suffered damage for My cause, and fought and were slain, verily I shall remit their evil deeds from them and verily I shall bring them into Gardens underneath which rivers flow - A reward from Allah. And with Allah is the fairest of rewards

12:34.ar: فَٱسۡتَجَابَ لَهُۥ رَبُّهُۥ فَصَرَفَ عَنۡهُ كَيۡدَهُنَّۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ
12:34.en: So his Lord heard his prayer and fended off their wiles from him. Lo! He is Hearer, Knower

13:14.ar: لَهُۥ دَعۡوَةُ ٱلۡحَقِّۚ وَٱلَّذِينَ يَدۡعُونَ مِن دُونِهِۦ لَا يَسۡتَجِيبُونَ لَهُم بِشَيۡءٍ إِلَّا كَبَٰسِطِ كَفَّيۡهِ إِلَى ٱلۡمَآءِ لِيَبۡلُغَ فَاهُ وَمَا هُوَ بِبَٰلِغِهِۦۚ وَمَا دُعَآءُ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ إِلَّا فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ‏
13:14.en: Unto Him is the real prayer. Those unto whom they pray beside Allah respond to them not at all, save as (is the response to) one who stretcheth forth his hands toward water (asking) that it may come unto his mouth, and it will never reach it. The prayer of disbelievers goeth (far) astray

28:64.ar: وَقِيلَ ٱدۡعُواْ شُرَكَآءَكُمۡ فَدَعَوۡهُمۡ فَلَمۡ يَسۡتَجِيبُواْ لَهُمۡ وَرَأَوُاْ ٱلۡعَذَابَۚ لَوۡ أَنَّهُمۡ كَانُواْ يَهۡتَدُونَ
28:64.en: And it will be said: Cry unto your (so-called) partners (of Allah). And they will cry unto them, and they will give no answer unto them, and they will see the Doom. Ah, if they had but been guided

35:14.ar: إِن تَدۡعُوهُمۡ لَا يَسۡمَعُواْ دُعَآءَكُمۡ وَلَوۡ سَمِعُواْ مَا ٱسۡتَجَابُواْ لَكُمۡۖ وَيَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ يَكۡفُرُونَ بِشِرۡكِكُمۡۚ وَلَا يُنَبِّئُكَ مِثۡلُ خَبِيرࣲ‏
35:14.en: If ye pray unto them they hear not your prayer, and if they heard they could not grant it you. On the Day of Resurrection they will disown association with you. None can inform you like Him Who is Aware

42:26.ar: وَيَسۡتَجِيبُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَيَزِيدُهُم مِّن فَضۡلِهِۦۚ وَٱلۡكَٰفِرُونَ لَهُمۡ عَذَابࣱ شَدِيدࣱ‏
42:26.en: And accepteth those who do good works, and giveth increase unto them of His bounty. And as for disbelievers, theirs will be an awful doom

6:36.ar: ۞إِنَّمَا يَسۡتَجِيبُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَسۡمَعُونَۘ وَٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰ يَبۡعَثُهُمُ ٱللَّهُ ثُمَّ إِلَيۡهِ يُرۡجَعُونَ
6:36.en: Only those can accept who hear. As for the dead, Allah will raise them up; then unto Him they will be returned

8:24.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱسۡتَجِيبُواْ لِلَّهِ وَلِلرَّسُولِ إِذَا دَعَاكُمۡ لِمَا يُحۡيِيكُمۡۖ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَحُولُ بَيۡنَ ٱلۡمَرۡءِ وَقَلۡبِهِۦ وَأَنَّهُۥٓ إِلَيۡهِ تُحۡشَرُونَ
8:24.en: O ye who believe! Obey Allah, and the messenger when He calleth you to that which quickeneth you, and know that Allah cometh in between the man and his own heart, and that He it is unto Whom ye will be gathered

42:38.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَجَابُواْ لِرَبِّهِمۡ وَأَقَامُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَأَمۡرُهُمۡ شُورَىٰ بَيۡنَهُمۡ وَمِمَّا رَزَقۡنَٰهُمۡ يُنفِقُونَ
42:38.en: And those who answer the call of their Lord and establish worship, and whose affairs are a matter of counsel, and who spend of what We have bestowed on them

13:18.ar: لِلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَجَابُواْ لِرَبِّهِمُ ٱلۡحُسۡنَىٰۚ وَٱلَّذِينَ لَمۡ يَسۡتَجِيبُواْ لَهُۥ لَوۡ أَنَّ لَهُم مَّا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ جَمِيعࣰ ا وَمِثۡلَهُۥ مَعَهُۥ لَٱفۡتَدَوۡاْ بِهِۦٓۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمۡ سُوٓءُ ٱلۡحِسَابِ وَمَأۡوَىٰهُمۡ جَهَنَّمُۖ وَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡمِهَادُ
13:18.en: For those who answered Allah's call is bliss; and for those who answered not His call, if they had all that is in the earth, and therewith the like thereof, they would proffer it as ransom. Such will have a woeful reckoning, and their habitation will be hell, a dire abode

14:22.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ لَمَّا قُضِيَ ٱلۡأَمۡرُ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ وَعَدَكُمۡ وَعۡدَ ٱلۡحَقِّ وَوَعَدتُّكُمۡ فَأَخۡلَفۡتُكُمۡۖ وَمَا كَانَ لِيَ عَلَيۡكُم مِّن سُلۡطَٰنٍ إِلَّآ أَن دَعَوۡتُكُمۡ فَٱسۡتَجَبۡتُمۡ لِيۖ فَلَا تَلُومُونِي وَلُومُوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۖ مَّآ أَنَا۠ بِمُصۡرِخِكُمۡ وَمَآ أَنتُم بِمُصۡرِخِيَّ إِنِّي كَفَرۡتُ بِمَآ أَشۡرَكۡتُمُونِ مِن قَبۡلُۗ إِنَّ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ لَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمࣱ‏
14:22.en: And Satan saith, when the matter hath been decided: Lo! Allah promised you a promise of truth; and I promised you, then failed you. And I had no power over you save that I called unto you and ye obeyed me. So blame not, but blame yourselves. I cannot help you, nor can ye help me, Lo! I disbelieved in that which ye before ascribed to me. Lo! for wrong-doers is a painful doom

17:52.ar: يَوۡمَ يَدۡعُوكُمۡ فَتَسۡتَجِيبُونَ بِحَمۡدِهِۦ وَتَظُنُّونَ إِن لَّبِثۡتُمۡ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣰ ا
17:52.en: A day when He will call you and ye will answer with His praise, and ye will think that ye have tarried but a little while

40:60.ar: وَقَالَ رَبُّكُمُ ٱدۡعُونِيٓ أَسۡتَجِبۡ لَكُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَسۡتَكۡبِرُونَ عَنۡ عِبَادَتِي سَيَدۡخُلُونَ جَهَنَّمَ دَاخِرِينَ
40:60.en: And your Lord hath said: Pray unto Me and I will hear your prayer. Lo! those who scorn My service, they will enter hell, disgraced

27:62.ar: أَمَّن يُجِيبُ ٱلۡمُضۡطَرَّ إِذَا دَعَاهُ وَيَكۡشِفُ ٱلسُّوٓءَ وَيَجۡعَلُكُمۡ خُلَفَآءَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِۗ أَءِلَٰهࣱ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِۚ قَلِيلࣰ ا مَّا تَذَكَّرُونَ
27:62.en: Is not He (best) Who answereth the wronged one when he crieth unto Him and removeth the evil, and hath made you viceroys of the earth? Is there any Allah beside Allah? Little do they reflect

C7YRNlAIpVA.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: Al-Mujeeb (The One Who Responds)
C7YRNlAIpVA.one_line: Al-Mujeeb in the Quran, why dua is an obligation, the forms Allah's response takes, and how to make dua without the social mask.
C7YRNlAIpVA.summary: This session on the Names of support and aid takes up Al-Mujeeb and ties it to Ramadan through the verse that Allah is near and answers the caller. He sorts the Quranic uses of the verb of responding into categories: Allah responding to the prophets in their distress, the inability of idols and false partners to respond, the believers responding to their Lord, Shaytan's disowning speech on Judgment Day, and humanity answering the final call. Because responding is His name, he argues, dua is not optional but an obligation, and he illustrates its power with the story of Abu Hurayrah's mother accepting Islam after the Prophet prayed for her. He then explains that Allah always responds, but in different forms: granting the request, giving something better, delaying it, averting a harm, or storing it for the Hereafter. The real value of dua is that it lays out your priorities, fears and plans before Allah, and it is therapeutic to hear yourself say them. He urges people to learn the art of dua this Ramadan, to come to Allah without titles or social front, admitting vulnerability, especially in sujud. He closes with three ways to live the name: respond to Allah yourself, be the answer to someone else's dua, and supplicate with certainty.

outline.heading: Al-Mujeeb in the Quran: near and responsive
outline.gist: The name and its verb occur often in the Quran; Allah describes Himself as near and answering, which links the name to the Ramadan verses on dua.

outline.heading: First category: Allah's response to the prophets
outline.gist: Ayyub, Nuh, Yunus, Zakariya and Yusuf each called on Allah and He responded by removing their hardship or temptation.

outline.heading: Second category: idols cannot respond
outline.gist: Those called upon besides Allah are like a person reaching for his reflection in water; on Judgment Day the partners will not answer.

outline.heading: Third category: the believers respond to their Lord
outline.gist: Only those who truly listen respond; responding to Allah and His Messenger gives life to the spirit, and those who refuse could not ransom themselves with the earth.

outline.heading: Shaytan's speech and the final call
outline.gist: Shaytan will say he only called and people answered; on the Last Day people will answer Allah's call and feel they lived only briefly.

outline.heading: Dua is an obligation because of this name
outline.gist: Allah commands people to call on Him and warns those too arrogant to do so; since His name is the One who responds, failing to supplicate is a fault.

outline.heading: Abu Hurayrah's mother and the Prophet's dua
outline.gist: After years of rejection, the Prophet prayed for her guidance and she accepted Islam that same day; then he prayed that believers love Abu Hurayrah and his mother.

outline.heading: Ramadan teaches us to supplicate again
outline.gist: Ramadan restores the habit of dua, and every dua is a direct experience of this name; one is always living one of Allah's names.

outline.heading: The forms Allah's response takes
outline.gist: He may grant the request, give something better, give it later, avert a coming harm, or keep it for forgiveness and higher rank in the Hereafter.

outline.heading: Why ask if the answer may differ
outline.gist: Response is guaranteed in whatever form Allah chooses; dua shows Allah your plan and mindset, and the fasting person has a dua that is not rejected.

outline.heading: Rejected duas and the postponed answer
outline.gist: Dua without sincerity or certainty can be rejected; a report of a pious servant whose answer was delayed because Allah loved hearing his voice shows that getting what we want often ends the conversation.

outline.heading: Dua reveals who you are
outline.gist: People ask for what they care most about, so dua explains their priorities and fears to Allah, and hearing oneself say them is therapeutic.

outline.heading: Certainty and the art of dua
outline.gist: Allah does not answer a distracted, indifferent heart; dua is a skill to learn this Ramadan and can become the most enjoyable act of one's life.

outline.heading: Come to Allah without the social mask
outline.gist: Titles, status and possessions mean nothing before Allah; come to Him now with the simplicity of a servant so the Day of Judgment is not the first time.

outline.heading: Drop the act; dua in sujud
outline.gist: Everyone is vulnerable and no one has life figured out; speak to Allah honestly, not like a job interview, and make dua with your face on the ground.

outline.heading: Living the name: respond to Allah yourself
outline.gist: If you want Allah to answer you, answer His call first.

outline.heading: Living the name: be the answer to someone's dua
outline.gist: Allah answers people through other people; being the means of someone's relief may be the best thing you ever do.

outline.heading: Living the name: supplicate with certainty
outline.gist: Make dua with full certainty that He will respond, accepting whatever form the response takes.

themes.note: Traces Al-Mujeeb through the Quran by the categories in which the verb of responding is used.

themes.label: Ramadan: preparation, fasting, making the most of it

themes.label: Humility vs vanity and arrogance
themes.note: Approach Allah stripped of titles and social front, as a vulnerable servant, ideally in sujud.

themes.label: Community building, cooperation and the ummah

6:17.ar: وَإِن يَمۡسَسۡكَ ٱللَّهُ بِضُرࣲّ فَلَا كَاشِفَ لَهُۥٓ إِلَّا هُوَۖ وَإِن يَمۡسَسۡكَ بِخَيۡرࣲ فَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ‏
6:17.en: If Allah touch thee with affliction, there is none that can relieve therefrom save Him, and if He touch thee with good fortune (there is none that can impair it); for He is Able to do all things

6:51.ar: وَأَنذِرۡ بِهِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخَافُونَ أَن يُحۡشَرُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِمۡ لَيۡسَ لَهُم مِّن دُونِهِۦ وَلِيࣱّ وَلَا شَفِيعࣱ لَّعَلَّهُمۡ يَتَّقُونَ
6:51.en: Warn hereby those who fear (because they know) that they will be gathered unto their Lord, for whom there is no protecting ally nor intercessor beside Him, that they may ward off (evil)

6:73.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ بِٱلۡحَقِّۖ وَيَوۡمَ يَقُولُ كُن فَيَكُونُۚ قَوۡلُهُ ٱلۡحَقُّۚ وَلَهُ ٱلۡمُلۡكُ يَوۡمَ يُنفَخُ فِي ٱلصُّورِۚ عَٰلِمُ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَٱلشَّهَٰدَةِۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ ٱلۡخَبِيرُ
6:73.en: He it is Who created the heavens and the earth in truth. In the day when He saith: Be! it is. His Word is the Truth, and His will be the Sovereignty on the day when the trumpet is blown. Knower of the Invisible and the Visible, He is the Wise, the Aware

6:118.ar: فَكُلُواْ مِمَّا ذُكِرَ ٱسۡمُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيۡهِ إِن كُنتُم بِـَٔايَٰتِهِۦ مُؤۡمِنِينَ
6:118.en: Eat of that over which the name of Allah hath been mentioned, if ye are believers in His revelations

6:136.ar: وَجَعَلُواْ لِلَّهِ مِمَّا ذَرَأَ مِنَ ٱلۡحَرۡثِ وَٱلۡأَنۡعَٰمِ نَصِيبࣰ ا فَقَالُواْ هَٰذَا لِلَّهِ بِزَعۡمِهِمۡ وَهَٰذَا لِشُرَكَآئِنَاۖ فَمَا كَانَ لِشُرَكَآئِهِمۡ فَلَا يَصِلُ إِلَى ٱللَّهِۖ وَمَا كَانَ لِلَّهِ فَهُوَ يَصِلُ إِلَىٰ شُرَكَآئِهِمۡۗ سَآءَ مَا يَحۡكُمُونَ
6:136.en: They assign unto Allah, of the crops and cattle which He created, a portion, and they say: "This is Allah's" - in their make-believe - "and this is for (His) partners in regard to us." Thus that which (they assign) unto His partners in them reacheth not Allah and that which (they assign) unto Allah goeth to their (so-called) partners. Evil is their ordinance

6:151.ar: ۞قُلۡ تَعَالَوۡاْ أَتۡلُ مَا حَرَّمَ رَبُّكُمۡ عَلَيۡكُمۡۖ أَلَّا تُشۡرِكُواْ بِهِۦ شَيۡـࣰٔ اۖ وَبِٱلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ إِحۡسَٰنࣰ اۖ وَلَا تَقۡتُلُوٓاْ أَوۡلَٰدَكُم مِّنۡ إِمۡلَٰقࣲ نَّحۡنُ نَرۡزُقُكُمۡ وَإِيَّاهُمۡۖ وَلَا تَقۡرَبُواْ ٱلۡفَوَٰحِشَ مَا ظَهَرَ مِنۡهَا وَمَا بَطَنَۖ وَلَا تَقۡتُلُواْ ٱلنَّفۡسَ ٱلَّتِي حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا بِٱلۡحَقِّۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ وَصَّىٰكُم بِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَعۡقِلُونَ
6:151.en: Say: Come, I will recite unto you that which your Lord hath made a sacred duty for you: That ye ascribe no thing as partner unto Him and that ye do good to parents, and that ye slay not your children because of penury - We provide for you and for them - and that ye draw not nigh to lewd things whether open or concealed. And that ye slay not the life which Allah hath made sacred, save in the course of justice. This He hath command you, in order that ye may discern

6:152.ar: وَلَا تَقۡرَبُواْ مَالَ ٱلۡيَتِيمِ إِلَّا بِٱلَّتِي هِيَ أَحۡسَنُ حَتَّىٰ يَبۡلُغَ أَشُدَّهُۥۚ وَأَوۡفُواْ ٱلۡكَيۡلَ وَٱلۡمِيزَانَ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِۖ لَا نُكَلِّفُ نَفۡسًا إِلَّا وُسۡعَهَاۖ وَإِذَا قُلۡتُمۡ فَٱعۡدِلُواْ وَلَوۡ كَانَ ذَا قُرۡبَىٰۖ وَبِعَهۡدِ ٱللَّهِ أَوۡفُواْۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ وَصَّىٰكُم بِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَذَكَّرُونَ
6:152.en: And approach not the wealth of the orphan save with that which is better, till he reach maturity. Give full measure and full weight, in justice. We task not any soul beyond its scope. And if ye give your word, do justice thereunto, even though it be (against) a kinsman; and fulfil the covenant of Allah. This He commandeth you that haply ye may remember

6:153.ar: وَأَنَّ هَٰذَا صِرَٰطِي مُسۡتَقِيمࣰ ا فَٱتَّبِعُوهُۖ وَلَا تَتَّبِعُواْ ٱلسُّبُلَ فَتَفَرَّقَ بِكُمۡ عَن سَبِيلِهِۦۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ وَصَّىٰكُم بِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَتَّقُونَ
6:153.en: And (He commandeth you, saying): This is My straight path, so follow it. Follow not other ways, lest ye be parted from His way. This hath He ordained for you, that ye may ward off (evil)

49:14.ar: ۞قَالَتِ ٱلۡأَعۡرَابُ ءَامَنَّاۖ قُل لَّمۡ تُؤۡمِنُواْ وَلَٰكِن قُولُوٓاْ أَسۡلَمۡنَا وَلَمَّا يَدۡخُلِ ٱلۡإِيمَٰنُ فِي قُلُوبِكُمۡۖ وَإِن تُطِيعُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ لَا يَلِتۡكُم مِّنۡ أَعۡمَٰلِكُمۡ شَيۡـًٔاۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمٌ
49:14.en: The wandering Arabs say: We believe. Say (unto them, O Muhammad): Ye believe not, but rather say "We submit," for the faith hath not yet entered into your hearts. Yet, if ye obey Allah and His messenger, He will not withhold from you aught of (the reward of) your deeds. Lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

2:286.ar: لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفۡسًا إِلَّا وُسۡعَهَاۚ لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتۡ وَعَلَيۡهَا مَا ٱكۡتَسَبَتۡۗ رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذۡنَآ إِن نَّسِينَآ أَوۡ أَخۡطَأۡنَاۚ رَبَّنَا وَلَا تَحۡمِلۡ عَلَيۡنَآ إِصۡرࣰ ا كَمَا حَمَلۡتَهُۥ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِنَاۚ رَبَّنَا وَلَا تُحَمِّلۡنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِۦۖ وَٱعۡفُ عَنَّا وَٱغۡفِرۡ لَنَا وَٱرۡحَمۡنَآۚ أَنتَ مَوۡلَىٰنَا فَٱنصُرۡنَا عَلَى ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
2:286.en: Allah tasketh not a soul beyond its scope. For it (is only) that which it hath earned, and against it (only) that which it hath deserved. Our Lord! Condemn us not if we forget, or miss the mark! Our Lord! Lay not on us such a burden as thou didst lay on those before us! Our Lord! Impose not on us that which we have not the strength to bear! Pardon us, absolve us and have mercy on us, Thou, our Protector, and give us victory over the disbelieving folk

16:116.ar: وَلَا تَقُولُواْ لِمَا تَصِفُ أَلۡسِنَتُكُمُ ٱلۡكَذِبَ هَٰذَا حَلَٰلࣱ وَهَٰذَا حَرَامࣱ لِّتَفۡتَرُواْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ ٱلۡكَذِبَۚ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَفۡتَرُونَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ ٱلۡكَذِبَ لَا يُفۡلِحُونَ
16:116.en: And speak not, concerning that which your own tongues qualify (as clean or unclean), the falsehood: "This is lawful, and this is forbidden," so that ye invent a lie against Allah. Lo! those who invent a lie against Allah will not succeed

voUK2jv0dEU.title: Ramadan 2024 Night 7: Quranic Reflections on Surat Al-An'am
voUK2jv0dEU.one_line: Al-An'am as the surah of iman: knowing Allah in its first half, proving it through obedience in its second, ending in the straight path.
voUK2jv0dEU.summary: He presents Al-An'am as a surah revealed in one piece about iman, which he insists is not mere belief but the internalising of truths until they drive behaviour. Its first half describes Allah so we know whom we obey; its second half, from 6:118, turns to commands, starting with food because eating is the most frequent and detailed of our behaviours. From 6:17 he notes that Allah only lets us be touched by hardship or good because we could not carry a full dose, and that knowing only He removes harm, while we still exhaust every means, cures much anxiety. From 6:51 he separates fearing a tyrant's oppression from fearing Allah's justice, which is why believers ask for His grace instead. From 6:73 he argues that a day in the Quran is a span of time and that the command to be need not mean instantly, as the long history of the universe shows. From 6:136 he shows how invented religious rules funnel wealth to clergy and rulers, and from 6:151-153 he calls people to the straight, incorruptible path rather than the many side roads.

outline.heading: Opening
The first eight surahs tell the story of the faith
outline.gist: Recap of the cluster: the job, the method, protection, values and the contract, with the rest of the Quran adding detail.

outline.heading: A surah revealed all at once
outline.gist: Scholars accept the report partly because the surah keeps one tone and rhythm from start to finish.

outline.heading: Iman is not belief
outline.gist: Iman means moving a truth from the surface of the mind into the deep consciousness where it governs behaviour.

outline.heading: First half of iman: knowing who Allah is
outline.gist: Accepting and understanding the theology, which grows by contemplating Allah's names.

outline.heading: Second half of iman: behaviour as the only evidence
outline.gist: No one can measure iman directly; actions are the proof, and without either half the relationship is incomplete.

outline.heading: Two halves of the surah and the symbol of livestock
outline.gist: The first half describes Allah, the second gives commands; livestock stand for all of Allah's blessings and what we do with them.

outline.heading: Verses that describe Allah
outline.gist: Of all the Quran he loves most the passages that describe Allah's majesty.

outline.heading: Find your own gateway into the Quran
outline.gist: Each person connects to different parts, stories or reminders of Paradise and Hell; holding on to that part lets you always find your way back.

outline.heading: Interlude
Only a touch of harm or good
outline.gist: The word for touch means the slightest contact; Allah gives only a whiff of hardship or good.

outline.heading: We could not bear half a dose
outline.gist: A half dose of hardship would break our faith and a half dose of wealth or fame would ruin us.

outline.heading: Grateful that we are not overburdened
outline.gist: That Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity is a law, and still a reason for gratitude.

outline.heading: Harm, not punishment; the same word for good and bad
outline.gist: Allah speaks of harm rather than punishment, and ease can turn out good or bad depending on its use.

outline.heading: Only Allah removes hardship
outline.gist: Seek doctors, help and loans as required effort, but know that He alone lifts difficulty and no one can block His bounty.

outline.heading: Certainty as a cure for anxiety
outline.gist: Knowing that what is meant for you will reach you makes a person calmer, steadier and unwilling to break rules.

outline.heading: Fearing Allah's justice, not oppression
outline.gist: The Quran warns those who fear meeting their Lord; people fear tyrants' injustice, but with Allah they fear receiving what they deserve.

outline.heading: Two kinds of fear a child feels
outline.gist: Fear of a harsh father differs from fear of a just one you hope to win over; hence asking Allah to deal with us by His grace.

outline.heading: No ally or intercessor besides Him
outline.gist: Without Allah as your ally you stand alone, and with Him you are never alone; intercession happens only by His leave.

outline.heading: A verse that holds the whole message
outline.gist: As a child he resented this verse appearing in every creed book; later he saw it covers warning, revelation, accountability and piety.

outline.heading: Created the heavens and earth in truth
outline.gist: The phrase can mean by, for or through truth, and every rendering is correct.

outline.heading: A day means a span of time
outline.gist: The Arabic word for day means a portion of time, so the six days of creation are not earthly days.

outline.heading: Be, and it is, in the way He intends
outline.gist: Nothing says it must be instant; the universe unfolded over billions of years from one command, like a cascade of dominoes.

outline.heading: Sovereign on the day the horn is blown
outline.gist: Allah owns all sovereignty at both blasts and knows the seen, the unseen and what is in hearts.

outline.heading: Answering His invitation in Ramadan
outline.gist: This is the Lord who invites you closer each night of Ramadan, so know whom you are answering and come running.

outline.heading: The surah changes gears to commands
outline.gist: After 117 verses on knowing Allah, a Makkan surah breaks pattern with rulings so belief can be proven in action.

outline.heading: Why food is the test
outline.gist: Eating is daily, detailed and varied, so accepting Allah's rules there shows iman reaches every part of life.

outline.heading: Shares for Allah and shares for idols
outline.gist: The pagans invented a system allotting crops and livestock to Allah and to idols, letting Allah's share flow to the idols but not the reverse.

outline.heading: No one may invent a ruling
outline.gist: Even rules that seem more pious are forbidden if Allah did not command them.

outline.heading: For Allah means for the needy
outline.gist: What is given to Allah reaches the poor and orphans, while the idols' share fed the clergy.

outline.heading: How clergy, wealth and rulers ruin a faith
outline.gist: Wealthy clergy attract rulers, manipulate people, and preserve the oppressor's status quo while the common person suffers.

outline.heading: Do not call things halal or haram falsely
outline.gist: Declaring what is lawful and unlawful belongs to Allah alone and demands the utmost care.

outline.heading: Our version of the Ten Commandments
outline.gist: Verses 151-153 parallel what Musa received, each closing with Allah's final advice.

outline.heading: The straight path is incorruptible
outline.gist: Knowing Allah results in a straight path with no shortcuts or corruption; iman that leaves you corrupt was placed in the wrong lord.

outline.heading: Side roads that divide and mislead
outline.gist: Countless other ways of living pull people apart and make them lose their attachment to Allah's way.

themes.label: Relationship with the Quran: reading, reflecting, living it

IshjJz8R5Vg.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: Malik al-Mulk (The Owner of All Kings)
IshjJz8R5Vg.one_line: Al-Malik and Malik al-Mulk: Allah owns everything including us, so He cannot oppress, earthly power is a brief loan, and we serve within His kingdom.
IshjJz8R5Vg.summary: Opening the category of names of domination, he treats the variants of Al-Malik as one name and ties it to Surat an-Nas, where Allah is described as Lord, King and God: He cares for us, deserves worship, and owns us. That ownership, he argues, is total, over body and soul, which is why no human can truly own another or anything at all. It also explains why Allah cannot oppress: oppression means taking what is not yours or breaking rules, and He owns everything and sets every rule. He surveys verses where false gods own nothing, not even the skin of a date stone, and verses where Allah lends kingship to people such as Namrud, the family of Ibrahim, Dawud and Sulayman, noting that earthly kings are quickly forgotten. Possessions remain His even when paid off and pass out of our control at death. Kingship sought for its own sake loses its blessing, as with Iblis's temptation of Adam and Pharaoh's boast before he drowned. On the Last Day Allah alone will declare Himself King. He asks people to grasp that being a servant means being owned, to act carefully within His kingdom and its protected boundaries, and to remember that rulers will answer for every bit of power they held.

outline.heading: Opening
Names of domination: Al-Malik as an umbrella name
outline.gist: From the many names of domination he chooses Al-Malik and its variants Malik and Malik al-Mulk, treating them as one name.

outline.heading: Lord, God and King in Surat an-Nas
outline.gist: The Quran ends by defining the relationship: Allah raises and cares for us, is the one worthy of worship, and is our King.

outline.heading: Allah owns us, so no one can own another
outline.gist: Despite the word's misuse in history, ownership is the true description: we already have an owner, body and soul, so human ownership of people or things makes no real sense.

outline.heading: Surat al-Mulk: the first thing to know
outline.gist: Allah is the Holy King, and Surat al-Mulk begins its lesson on what a caller to Islam must know with His sovereignty over everything.

outline.heading: Why Allah cannot oppress
outline.gist: Oppression means putting something where it does not belong or violating another's rights; since Allah owns everything and makes all the rules, oppression from Him is impossible, even if He punished prophets.

outline.heading: To Him belongs the kingdom of the heavens and earth
outline.gist: Repeated many times in the Quran; He owns our hearing and sight and can take them back, so where is our mindfulness of Him?

outline.heading: Malik al-Mulk: owner of every king
outline.gist: Allah gives and removes kingship and honour as He wills; every king is His property.

outline.heading: False gods own nothing
outline.gist: They own neither life, death, benefit nor harm, not the thin skin of a date stone, not an atom, and not even the right to speak or intercede.

outline.heading: Namrud: kingship lent for a moment
outline.gist: The man who argued with Ibrahim did so only because Allah had given him rule over a small land, few people and a short time.

outline.heading: Earthly kings are forgotten
outline.gist: No one remembers the succession of past dynasties; a king's power means little.

outline.heading: Kingdom granted to Ibrahim's family, Dawud and Sulayman
outline.gist: Allah uses the same word when He grants sovereignty to His prophets, and He gives and takes it as He wills.

outline.heading: You own nothing, even what is paid off
outline.gist: Possessions are with us temporarily; at death wealth is distributed as Allah decrees, and accepting this changes how we react to gain and loss.

outline.heading: Kingship sought loses its blessing: Iblis and Adam
outline.gist: Iblis tempted Adam with a kingdom that never decays; control attracts us though we were not made for it.

outline.heading: Pharaoh's boast and drowning
outline.gist: He claimed the rivers flowed beneath him, so Allah made the sea flow over his head.

outline.heading: The kingdom on the Day of Judgment and in Jannah
outline.gist: Allah asks whose kingdom it is that Day and answers Himself; in Paradise the believer will see a great kingdom beyond imagination.

outline.heading: I am the King: folding the heavens and the nightly descent
outline.gist: Allah folds the heavens and earth and asks where the tyrants are; in the last third of the night He calls who will ask so He may give.

outline.heading: Every king has a protected land
outline.gist: Allah's protected boundary is what He made haram; the rest of the earth is made easy for us to enjoy, though it is not ours.

outline.heading: Living the name: understand you are owned
outline.gist: Being a servant means having an owner and results in service; real liberty among people rests on knowing Allah owns us all.

outline.heading: Living the name: tread carefully in His kingdom
outline.gist: Everything you touch is His, so check that the Owner of Kings approves before you act; those who oppress will stand before the Master of the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: A king's reign is brief and accountable
outline.gist: A few decades of power is nothing; even just rulers enter Paradise long after the poor because they must answer for what they held.

themes.label: The Names and Attributes of Allah
themes.note: Al-Malik and Malik al-Mulk traced through the Quran and hadith as total ownership and sovereignty.

themes.label: Justice and refusing oppression
themes.note: Oppression cannot come from Allah because He owns everything; people oppress by acting as owners.

themes.label: Wealth, asceticism (zuhd), consumerism and money
themes.note: Possessions are temporary trusts; at death we lose control of them entirely.

themes.label: Leadership, governance and institutions
themes.note: Kingship is lent briefly by Allah; seeking it for itself removes its blessing, as with Pharaoh.

themes.label: Humility vs vanity and arrogance
themes.note: We are servants, not owners; rulers must answer for their power and enter Paradise late.

themes.label: Freedom, rights and responsibility
themes.note: Individual liberties matter as barriers between people, and they rest on knowing Allah owns us all.

themes.label: Accountability before Allah and goals
themes.note: Everyone will be asked what they did with the power they were given.

13:11.ar: لَهُۥ مُعَقِّبَٰتࣱ مِّنۢ بَيۡنِ يَدَيۡهِ وَمِنۡ خَلۡفِهِۦ يَحۡفَظُونَهُۥ مِنۡ أَمۡرِ ٱللَّهِۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُغَيِّرُ مَا بِقَوۡمٍ حَتَّىٰ يُغَيِّرُواْ مَا بِأَنفُسِهِمۡۗ وَإِذَآ أَرَادَ ٱللَّهُ بِقَوۡمࣲ سُوٓءࣰ ا فَلَا مَرَدَّ لَهُۥۚ وَمَا لَهُم مِّن دُونِهِۦ مِن وَالٍ
13:11.en: For him are angels ranged before him and behind him, who guard him by Allah's command. Lo! Allah changeth not the condition of a folk until they (first) change that which is in their hearts; and if Allah willeth misfortune for a folk there is none that can repel it, nor have they a defender beside Him

13:12.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي يُرِيكُمُ ٱلۡبَرۡقَ خَوۡفࣰ ا وَطَمَعࣰ ا وَيُنشِئُ ٱلسَّحَابَ ٱلثِّقَالَ
13:12.en: He it is Who showeth you the lightning, a fear and a hope, and raiseth the heavy clouds

13:13.ar: وَيُسَبِّحُ ٱلرَّعۡدُ بِحَمۡدِهِۦ وَٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ مِنۡ خِيفَتِهِۦ وَيُرۡسِلُ ٱلصَّوَٰعِقَ فَيُصِيبُ بِهَا مَن يَشَآءُ وَهُمۡ يُجَٰدِلُونَ فِي ٱللَّهِ وَهُوَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡمِحَالِ
13:13.en: The thunder hymneth His praise and (so do) the angels for awe of Him. He launcheth the thunderbolts and smiteth with them whom He will while they dispute (in doubt) concerning Allah, and He is mighty in wrath

13:14.ar: لَهُۥ دَعۡوَةُ ٱلۡحَقِّۚ وَٱلَّذِينَ يَدۡعُونَ مِن دُونِهِۦ لَا يَسۡتَجِيبُونَ لَهُم بِشَيۡءٍ إِلَّا كَبَٰسِطِ كَفَّيۡهِ إِلَى ٱلۡمَآءِ لِيَبۡلُغَ فَاهُ وَمَا هُوَ بِبَٰلِغِهِۦۚ وَمَا دُعَآءُ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ إِلَّا فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ‏
13:14.en: Unto Him is the real prayer. Those unto whom they pray beside Allah respond to them not at all, save as (is the response to) one who stretcheth forth his hands toward water (asking) that it may come unto his mouth, and it will never reach it. The prayer of disbelievers goeth (far) astray

13:8.ar: ٱللَّهُ يَعۡلَمُ مَا تَحۡمِلُ كُلُّ أُنثَىٰ وَمَا تَغِيضُ ٱلۡأَرۡحَامُ وَمَا تَزۡدَادُۚ وَكُلُّ شَيۡءٍ عِندَهُۥ بِمِقۡدَارٍ
13:8.en: Allah knoweth that which every female beareth and that which the wombs absorb and that which they grow. And everything with Him is measured

13:9.en: He is the Knower of the Invisible and the Visible, the Great, the High Exalted

13:10.ar: سَوَآءࣱ مِّنكُم مَّنۡ أَسَرَّ ٱلۡقَوۡلَ وَمَن جَهَرَ بِهِۦ وَمَنۡ هُوَ مُسۡتَخۡفِۭ بِٱلَّيۡلِ وَسَارِبُۢ بِٱلنَّهَارِ
13:10.en: Alike of you is he who hideth the saying and he who noiseth it abroad, he who lurketh in the night and he who goeth freely in the daytime

17:14.ar: ٱقۡرَأۡ كِتَٰبَكَ كَفَىٰ بِنَفۡسِكَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ عَلَيۡكَ حَسِيبࣰ ا
17:14.en: (And it will be said unto him): Read thy Book. Thy soul sufficeth as reckoner against thee this day

106:2.en: For their taming (We cause) the caravans to set forth in winter and summer

2:214.ar: أَمۡ حَسِبۡتُمۡ أَن تَدۡخُلُواْ ٱلۡجَنَّةَ وَلَمَّا يَأۡتِكُم مَّثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ خَلَوۡاْ مِن قَبۡلِكُمۖ مَّسَّتۡهُمُ ٱلۡبَأۡسَآءُ وَٱلضَّرَّآءُ وَزُلۡزِلُواْ حَتَّىٰ يَقُولَ ٱلرَّسُولُ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مَعَهُۥ مَتَىٰ نَصۡرُ ٱللَّهِۗ أَلَآ إِنَّ نَصۡرَ ٱللَّهِ قَرِيبࣱ‏
2:214.en: Or think ye that ye will enter paradise while yet there hath not come unto you the like of (that which came to) those who passed away before you? Affliction and adversity befell them, they were shaken as with earthquake, till the messenger (of Allah) and those who believed along with him said: When cometh Allah's help? Now surely Allah's help is nigh

17:44.ar: تُسَبِّحُ لَهُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ ٱلسَّبۡعُ وَٱلۡأَرۡضُ وَمَن فِيهِنَّۚ وَإِن مِّن شَيۡءٍ إِلَّا يُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِهِۦ وَلَٰكِن لَّا تَفۡقَهُونَ تَسۡبِيحَهُمۡۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ حَلِيمًا غَفُورࣰ ا
17:44.en: The seven heavens and the earth and all that is therein praise Him, and there is not a thing but hymneth His praise; but ye understand not their praise. Lo! He is ever Clement, Forgiving

NVKT-UksfHA.title: Tafsir of Surat Al-Ra'd, Part 3
NVKT-UksfHA.one_line: Explains 13:11-14: recording angels and self-judgment, the law that Allah does not change a people until they change, thunder, and false supplication.
NVKT-UksfHA.summary: After recapping the surah's focus on the laws Allah uses to run creation, he explains the angels who follow each person in succession, preserving every deed. Allah needs no records, but witnesses and a written book let people accept His verdict, so no one enters Hell feeling wronged and no one enters Paradise feeling they earned it; shown who Allah is and what they did, people judge themselves. He then reaches the law he says the surah revolves around: Allah does not change a people's state until they change themselves. In context it warned a comfortable Quraysh against losing their blessings, but as a general law it means the ummah will not rise without deep, widespread and sustained change. He calls the expectation of a sudden turnaround delusional, says it may take a generation or two, points to the Prophet's 23 years of struggle, and warns against plans that count on a miracle. History, including Muslims bombarding the Kaaba and the Mongol invasions, must be read honestly, bright and dark. He closes with lightning that brings fear and hope, thunder as audible evidence of unseen events and the reason for the surah's name, and the image of one who reaches for water to bring it to his mouth: calling on anyone besides Allah.

outline.heading: Recap: the laws Allah uses to govern His universe
outline.gist: The surah's first page lists facts of creation that we take for granted because they are constant.

outline.heading: Recap of 13:8-10: knowledge of wombs and secrets
outline.gist: Everything has its measure, and secret and open speech are equal to Allah.

outline.heading: People know only what is apparent; Allah knows hearts
outline.gist: Even surveillance cannot reach what is inside a heart, but to Allah the hidden and the open are the same.

outline.heading: Angels in succession before and behind each person
outline.gist: Mu'aqqibat are angels who follow up on each other, tracking everything a person has done and will do, by Allah's command.

outline.heading: Hifz as preservation: nothing goes unrecorded
outline.gist: Protecting, memorizing and observing all mean preserving; every deed is documented in your book.

outline.heading: Why angels record when Allah needs no record
outline.gist: Witnesses and a written book exist for us, because people do not accept a judgment without them.

outline.heading: No one enters Hell feeling wronged
outline.gist: Unlike prisoners who all claim innocence, people walking to Hell feel the verdict is beyond fair and only hoped for a pardon.

outline.heading: No one enters Paradise feeling they earned it
outline.gist: Everyone in Paradise feels they barely made it through Allah's forgiveness and multiplication of their deeds.

outline.heading: Shown the reality of Allah and of yourself
outline.gist: Confronted with who Allah is and what they did, people cannot understand how they lived without reverence or repentance.

outline.heading: Read your book: you will judge yourself
outline.gist: The record makes each person their own judge, and it preserves the good as well as the bad.

outline.heading: Allah does not change a people until they change themselves
outline.gist: The law the surah revolves around; in its wording it means Allah does not remove a good state until people change for the worse.

outline.heading: The original warning to Quraysh
outline.gist: Quraysh took their trade journeys and wealth for granted, turned from what was right and lost their authority.

outline.heading: The general law: no change without changing
outline.gist: Real achievement costs so much that it barely feels worth it, and what comes without effort is easily squandered.

outline.heading: Expecting a sudden turnaround is delusional
outline.gist: Allah is able to do anything, but He explained how change happens, so expecting the ummah to rise without sincere change ignores His word.

outline.heading: Hardship before victory: a generation or two of work
outline.gist: Even after people change, trials shake them until they ask when help will come; restoring dignity and unity will take generations.

outline.heading: The Prophet's 23 years of struggle
outline.gist: His path was persecution, exile, war and setbacks, not a smooth rising graph; respecting Allah's decree means respecting His laws.

outline.heading: Change takes the long road: medicine and family
outline.gist: Like medical training or raising a family, nothing comes cheaply; no generation rises until the one before it is spent.

outline.heading: Don't plan around a miracle
outline.gist: No sensible company plans for a law-breaking miracle midway; doing so means we have not read what Allah told us.

outline.heading: Muslims bombarded the Kaaba: read history honestly
outline.gist: Early Muslims besieged Mecca and broke the Kaaba; we must learn from what worked and what failed instead of painting history in one colour.

outline.heading: The Mongol invasions
outline.gist: The Mongol era was far worse than today; extreme events sometimes forced change before the ummah recovered.

outline.heading: Radical change in mentality, widely shared
outline.gist: Change must reach attitudes, perspectives and life goals, and many people must turn the wheel together.

outline.heading: If Allah wills hardship, none can repel it
outline.gist: No protector exists besides Allah; this law sits among the facts of creation as just as certain as they are.

outline.heading: Lightning brings fear and hope; thunder glorifies
outline.gist: Lightning frightens yet promises rain; Allah forms heavy clouds and the thunder praises Him.

outline.heading: Everything praises Allah in its own way
outline.gist: A physical explanation of thunder does not cancel its praise; tasbih here is each thing functioning as it was made to.

outline.heading: Why the surah is called Thunder
outline.gist: Thunder is a loud sign of something happening out of sight, as all events in the world point to Allah whom we do not see.

outline.heading: Angels in awe; thunderbolts; those who dispute about Allah
outline.gist: Angels glorify Him out of fear while people argue about His existence, power and wisdom.

outline.heading: Mighty in argument; the call of truth belongs to Him
outline.gist: Al-mihal can mean the strongest argument or great power; the true supplication belongs to Allah alone.

outline.heading: Reaching for water to bring it to your mouth
outline.gist: Calling on anyone besides Allah is like chasing a reflection; creation reflects Him, so turn and speak to Him directly.

13:1.ar: الٓمٓرۚ تِلۡكَ ءَايَٰتُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِۗ وَٱلَّذِيٓ أُنزِلَ إِلَيۡكَ مِن رَّبِّكَ ٱلۡحَقُّ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
13:1.en: Alif. Lam. Mim. Ra. These are verses of the Scripture. That which is revealed unto thee from thy Lord is the Truth, but most of mankind believe not

13:2.ar: ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي رَفَعَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ بِغَيۡرِ عَمَدࣲ تَرَوۡنَهَاۖ ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلۡعَرۡشِۖ وَسَخَّرَ ٱلشَّمۡسَ وَٱلۡقَمَرَۖ كُلࣱّ يَجۡرِي لِأَجَلࣲ مُّسَمࣰّ ىۚ يُدَبِّرُ ٱلۡأَمۡرَ يُفَصِّلُ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ لَعَلَّكُم بِلِقَآءِ رَبِّكُمۡ تُوقِنُونَ
13:2.en: Allah it is Who raised up the heavens without visible supports, then mounted the Throne, and compelled the sun and the moon to be of service, each runneth unto an appointed term; He ordereth the course; He detaileth the revelations, that haply ye may be certain of the meeting with your Lord

13:3.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي مَدَّ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا رَوَٰسِيَ وَأَنۡهَٰرࣰ اۖ وَمِن كُلِّ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ جَعَلَ فِيهَا زَوۡجَيۡنِ ٱثۡنَيۡنِۖ يُغۡشِي ٱلَّيۡلَ ٱلنَّهَارَۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
13:3.en: And He it is Who spread out the earth and placed therein firm hills and flowing streams, and of all fruits He placed therein two spouses (male and female). He covereth the night with the day. Lo! herein verily are portents for people who take thought

2:23.ar: وَإِن كُنتُمۡ فِي رَيۡبࣲ مِّمَّا نَزَّلۡنَا عَلَىٰ عَبۡدِنَا فَأۡتُواْ بِسُورَةࣲ مِّن مِّثۡلِهِۦ وَٱدۡعُواْ شُهَدَآءَكُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
2:23.en: And if ye are in doubt concerning that which We reveal unto Our slave (Muhammad), then produce a surah of the like thereof, and call your witness beside Allah if ye are truthful

Wbjz8hRZmY0.speaker_note: speaks of the weekend Ramadan surah series he has run for years and of memorizing poetry as a student in Syria
Wbjz8hRZmY0.title: Tafsir of Surat Al-Ra'd, Part 1
Wbjz8hRZmY0.one_line: Introduces Surat Al-Ra'd as the surah of the laws governing existence, the Quran's challenge to Arab eloquence, and explains 13:1-3.
Wbjz8hRZmY0.summary: He opens a weekend Ramadan series on Surat Al-Ra'd, which he calls underrated. He places it in a cluster of four surahs after the long ones, each protecting one piece without which the faith stops working: theology in Yunus, reform in Hud, consistent ethics in Yusuf, and in Al-Ra'd the laws that govern existence, above all the law of haqq. As a mid-to-late Meccan surah it shows what Allah asks of believers in hardship: values, perseverance and giving, while detailed laws came later in the ease of Medina. The disjointed letters are an implied challenge to the Arabs, whose one real strength was language; he digresses on their political disunity, argues the ummah must learn from its past mistakes rather than romanticize them, and tells how Quraysh leaders secretly listened to the Prophet's recitation and how Ka'b ibn Zuhayr won the Prophet's cloak through a poem full of symbolism. He then explains 13:1-3: the Quran as pure truth, heavens raised without pillars, the sun and moon subjected and running to a term, and the earth's mountains, rivers and alternating night and day. His key lesson is to build certainty on these constant laws, not on whether a dua was answered.

outline.heading: Opening
Al-Ra'd: an underrated surah after the long surahs
outline.gist: He loves Al-Ra'd for its profound verses and places it right after the eight long surahs that open the Quran.

outline.heading: Yunus and Hud: theology and reform as indispensable pieces
outline.gist: Four surahs from Yunus onward each guard one critical concept; without reform, Hud's subject, Islam becomes toothless and changes no behaviour.

outline.heading: Yusuf: an ethic must be consistent
outline.gist: A selective moral is not an ethic at all; values must hold across every situation.

outline.heading: Al-Ra'd: the laws that govern existence and the law of haqq
outline.gist: Al-Ra'd is about the laws of existence, not fiqh or physics; where Yunus sets haqq against aimlessness, Al-Ra'd sets it against falsehood.

outline.heading: Meccan and Medinan revelation by length and number
outline.gist: Most surahs are Meccan but the Quran by volume is split roughly in half between Mecca and Medina.

outline.heading: Meccan surahs show what Allah expects in hardship
outline.gist: Revealed during persecution, these surahs tell a struggling believer exactly what Allah wants from him in a hard time.

outline.heading: Values and giving in weakness, laws in strength
outline.gist: Perseverance and giving were demanded when Muslims had nothing; detailed laws came once they had strength, so people living in ease should already have their values settled.

outline.heading: Reciting the opening letters alif lam mim ra
outline.gist: No authentic occasion of revelation; he explains the elongation counts for the disjointed letters.

outline.heading: Disjointed letters: a code and an implied challenge
outline.gist: The letters link surahs with shared themes and dare the Arabs to produce something like the Quran from their own alphabet.

outline.heading: The Arabs never organized politically
outline.gist: Outside Islam the Arabs never built political unity; their kings were loyal to outside empires, as rulers today still are to West or East.

outline.heading: Learning from the ummah's political history
outline.gist: Fourteen centuries is early for a faith; romanticizing a turbulent past keeps us stuck, and a better system of representation needs honest revision.

outline.heading: Pre-Islamic poetry and Arab command of language
outline.gist: Their oratory was unparalleled, turning a landscape of sand and camels into rich symbolism.

outline.heading: The Quran breaks the rules of Arabic poetry
outline.gist: It ignored the rigid poetic metres, brought something artistic and philosophical, and openly mocked their inability to match it.

outline.heading: Quraysh leaders listening secretly at night
outline.gist: Abu Jahl, Abu Sufyan and another leader kept bumping into each other behind the Prophet's wall, drawn by recitation they publicly opposed.

outline.heading: Ka'b ibn Zuhayr comes to Medina in disguise
outline.gist: The son of the poet Zuhayr, a fugitive enemy, arrives veiled and recites a long poem that seems to be about a lost love and his camel.

outline.heading: The Prophet reads the symbolism and gives his cloak
outline.gist: The Prophet understood the poem as a plea from a man who had lost his status, and gave him his cloak, which honoured the family for centuries.

outline.heading: What was sent down to you is the truth
outline.gist: The surah goes straight to haqq; seeing the Quran as pure truth with no falsehood changes how you relate to it.

outline.heading: Heavens raised without pillars you can see
outline.gist: People imagined only pillars could hold something up; the cosmos is held by other laws.

outline.heading: Istiwa upon the throne without likening Allah to creation
outline.gist: Accepting the wording or interpreting it as dominance are both valid, provided no resemblance to creation is drawn.

outline.heading: Sun and moon subjected: creation in mutual service
outline.gist: Taskhir means placing something at another's service, as people serve one another through different roles.

outline.heading: Everything runs to an appointed term
outline.gist: Only Allah is infinite; the universe will reach an end, which fits current cosmology.

outline.heading: Certainty of meeting your Lord needs the unseen
outline.gist: If the unseen were seen, belief would lose its meaning; true certainty comes from reasoning about evidence.

outline.heading: Signs in the laws of creation lead to accountability
outline.gist: The finely tuned order of the cosmos points to Allah, and certainty that you will stand before Him and answer for your life.

outline.heading: Build iman on constant laws, not on answered duas
outline.gist: These laws break only on the Day of Judgment; faith resting on whether a dua was answered collapses like matchsticks.

outline.heading: The earth spread out: mountains, rivers, pairs, night and day
outline.gist: Mountains anchor the land, rivers make civilization possible, and the cycle of day and night makes life workable: signs for those who reflect.

TfkOASjtW8w.title: Ramadan 2024 Night 9: Quranic Reflections on Al-A'raf, Al-Anfal and At-Tawbah
TfkOASjtW8w.one_line: Closing the first cluster of surahs: reformers who hold others to the Book, the sudden Hour, effort and outcome, trials that expose, preparation and humility.
TfkOASjtW8w.summary: He completes his map of the first eight surahs as one story: humanity's role as stewards, the method, its protection, values, the contract, iman, communal decisiveness, the laws of victory in Al-Anfal and the organising of relations in At-Tawbah. Al-Anfal teaches success by critiquing the companions' mistakes at Badr, so any success should be followed by asking what went wrong. From 7:170 he stresses that the reward is promised to reformers who make others hold firmly to the Book, not to those who are merely pious alone. From 7:187 he insists the Hour comes suddenly and only Allah knows it, so every moment matters and predictions should not make people relax. From 8:17 he separates releasing the arrow, which is our job, from hitting the target, which is Allah's; suffering exists partly to see what we will do, and the ummah has not even begun trying. From 8:37 trials expose true scholars and leaders from the corrupt, and from 8:60 he reframes preparation today as knowledge, mentorship, advocacy, wealth and dawah. Hunayn closes the night: never let numbers or success go to your head.

outline.heading: Opening
Twelve clusters of surahs
outline.gist: He now counts twelve clusters in the Quran and treats Al-Fatihah as its own entity; the first runs from Al-Baqarah to At-Tawbah.

outline.heading: Communities obey through decisiveness
outline.gist: Individuals show iman through belief and practice; communities show it by caring, prioritising and taking firm stands.

outline.heading: Followers of the prophets who lacked decisiveness
outline.gist: In Al-A'raf the arrogant and disbelieving were decisive while the followers were not, which led to their ruin, Bani Israel above all.

outline.heading: Al-Anfal: the short surah of laws
outline.gist: Laws come concisely, so Al-Anfal is short among the long surahs, yet it sits there because of the story the cluster tells.

outline.heading: Laws of victory taught through Badr's mistakes
outline.gist: Unity, adherence to Allah's rulings, preparation, strong iman and advocacy are taught by pointing out what nearly went wrong at the moment of victory.

outline.heading: After success, look at what went wrong
outline.gist: Celebrating without review leaves no room to improve; if you are not getting better, you are getting worse.

outline.heading: At-Tawbah organises relations with others
outline.gist: The last surah of the cluster sets out how the nation deals with non-Muslim citizens, traitors, hostile nations and those at peace.

outline.heading: The story so far: steward, method, protection
outline.gist: You are a steward, Islam is the method, and Aal-Imran shows how to protect it from external and internal threats.

outline.heading: Values, contract and iman
outline.gist: An-Nisa gives the values, Al-Ma'idah the contract, Al-An'am the individual relationship with Allah.

outline.heading: Community, laws of victory and relationships
outline.gist: Al-A'raf turns iman into communal decisiveness, Al-Anfal gives the laws to succeed, and At-Tawbah organises relations with those around you.

outline.heading: Those who make others hold to the Book
outline.gist: The verb means holding firm and getting others to hold firm; establishing prayer symbolises establishing Allah's deen on earth.

outline.heading: Reformers, not only the righteous
outline.gist: A salih is good on his own; a muslih brings reform to others, and the reward is promised to the reformers.

outline.heading: Carrying the communal obligations
outline.gist: No verse promises reward for holding the Book alone; reformers fix deficits on behalf of the group.

outline.heading: We need far more reformers
outline.gist: Survival comes from strengthening others' grip on the Book and helping them establish prayer, not from private piety.

outline.heading: The prophets came to reform
outline.gist: Nuh, Hud, Salih and Lut each named what had to change, and those who stood with them were saved.

outline.heading: Your success means little if your society fails
outline.gist: Confront egocentric approaches to the deen so the community has unity and collaboration.

outline.heading: Knowledge of the Hour is with Allah alone
outline.gist: The Hour weighs heavily on the heavens and earth and comes only suddenly.

outline.heading: The Quran over hard-to-verify end-times reports
outline.gist: He prefers what the Quran says about the Hour to narrations that are hard to authenticate and often have a negative effect.

outline.heading: Interrupted in the middle of daily tasks
outline.gist: People mending a basin, trading a garment, carrying milk or lifting food to their mouth will not finish before the Hour strikes.

outline.heading: Live as if it could come any moment
outline.gist: Seeing the Hour as distant makes people relax; the Quran says you only have now, which makes time valuable.

outline.heading: The one asked knows no more than the asker
outline.gist: If the Prophet told Jibril he did not know the Hour's timing, others should stop predicting it.

outline.heading: You did not throw when you threw
outline.gist: After Badr, Allah tells the believers they did not kill the enemy, and that the throw was His, which seems contradictory at first.

outline.heading: Releasing the arrow versus hitting the target
outline.gist: The first verb means reaching the target, the second the act of release; we release, Allah makes it hit.

outline.heading: All you can do is release
outline.gist: Train hard, get good tools and focus, but the outcome is beyond you; the effort exists to test and prove you.

outline.heading: Let's see what you will do
outline.gist: Allah could feed the starving at any moment; the suffering is a test of whether you act.

outline.heading: Seeing every circumstance through this verse
outline.gist: Personal, national and international situations all ask what you will do with them.

outline.heading: We are three steps behind this verse
outline.gist: The verse speaks of when effort succeeds; the companions tried for thirteen years in Makkah before victory, while we have not yet tried.

outline.heading: Trials distinguish the rotten from the good
outline.gist: Without difficulty everyone looks great; sacrifice, swallowing ego and risk reveal who people are.

outline.heading: True scholar or wealth-seeker, leader or dictator
outline.gist: Only trials expose the difference, and it is Allah's job, not the imam's, to point out who is who.

outline.heading: Judgment needs evidence
outline.gist: Even with Allah's perfect knowledge, condemning someone who never did wrong would feel unfair without proof.

outline.heading: Do not be in the pile
outline.gist: Allah heaps the rotten together into Hell without dignity; life is about not ending up in that pile.

outline.heading: How to identify central verses
outline.gist: Central verses in surahs and clusters are recognised by their wording: generic commands with specific actions.

outline.heading: Prepare all the strength you can
outline.gist: Bringing your best deters those hostile to you and others you do not know of who might plan harm.

outline.heading: Spending means using things up for Allah
outline.gist: The word evokes a tunnel where something disappears; time, expertise and wealth spent for Allah are returned without loss.

outline.heading: Allah's interest on your giving
outline.gist: What you give is held and grows until you meet Him, the only interest that is allowed.

outline.heading: Preparation in our context
outline.gist: Not horses tied outside the masjid, but knowledge, mentorship, advocacy, wealth, outreach and dawah.

outline.heading: Hunayn: the all-or-nothing attack
outline.gist: After the conquest of Makkah, rival tribes went all in, believing it was now or never.

outline.heading: Pleased with their numbers, then they fled
outline.gist: The enemy brought families and livestock to keep men from fleeing; the Muslims, unusually close in numbers, grew vain and ran until Allah's grace returned them.

outline.heading: Never let anything go to your head
outline.gist: If Allah loves you He pulls the rug from under your vanity; otherwise He lets you believe you are what you are not.

0xwVu6Fc8VM.speaker_note: refers to his ten years as imam in the city and to the census he ran of all London masajid; his usual style
0xwVu6Fc8VM.title: Three Ramadanic Reminders
0xwVu6Fc8VM.one_line: Using a citywide taraweeh head-count, he gives three Ramadan reminders: renew your intention, invest in the youth Allah brought, and back dua with action.
0xwVu6Fc8VM.summary: He opens with a census he ran across the city's masajid: about 6,500 people pray taraweeh nightly in Ramadan, against roughly 400 the rest of the year, and most drop off afterwards. Only Allah can turn hearts that quickly, he argues, and this also explains why the Prophet's khutbahs were short: his community lived year-round the way ours lives only in Ramadan. Ramadan is a push Allah gives, but staying afterwards is our responsibility. He then gives three reminders. First, renew your intention every Jumuah of the month; if your relationship with Allah is not enough, do it for yourself, or for the tens of thousands killed in Gaza, because rituals were never meant to be cut off from the condition of the ummah. Second, he cautiously hopes the crowds signal a youth-driven awakening, notes that every revival in Muslim history was led by the young, and warns that masajid must open their minds and hearts, accepting young people with their flaws and doing the hard, unglamorous work of mentoring them, or they will leave. Third, asking Allah for victory while doing nothing toward it is disrespectful, so every such dua needs an action plan. He closes with Abu Hanifah's quiet rescue of his drunk neighbour, who became a scholar.

outline.heading: Opening
Respond to what gives you life (8:24)
outline.gist: Answer Allah and His Messenger when they call you to what gives you life, meaning spiritual life; Allah stands between you and your heart and you will be gathered to Him.

outline.heading: 6,500 in Ramadan, 400 outside it
outline.gist: He had every imam and centre manager estimate taraweeh attendance: about 6,500 nightly, the highest in his ten years, against about 400 outside Ramadan. A caller invites seekers of good to come near.

outline.heading: Only Allah turns hearts this fast
outline.gist: Who else could move a city from 400 to 6,500 in one night? Only the King of Kings, who holds His servants' hearts between two of His fingers.

outline.heading: Why the Prophet's khutbahs were short
outline.gist: His recorded khutbahs are concise, naming deficits and next steps, because his community lived year-round the way ours lives only in Ramadan.

outline.heading: Allah brought you; staying is your job
outline.gist: Attendance drops 70 to 80 percent after the month. Ramadan, with Paradise open and Shaytan chained, is a boost Allah gives; afterwards it is on you to keep coming and find your piece of the puzzle.

outline.heading: A full masjid needs only a short reminder
outline.gist: When people are already volunteering, reading and serving, a brief pointer is enough; after Ramadan the drop-off forces long appeals to come back. He sets out three reminders.

outline.heading: Reminder one: renew your intention
outline.gist: Every Jumuah of the month is a milestone for renewing intention. Fasting while working or studying and standing at night take a toll, so know why you are doing it.

outline.heading: Do it for the people of Gaza
outline.gist: If Allah's love is not enough, do it for yourself, or for the 31,000 killed under the rubble of their homes for sharing your faith and refusing to leave their land.

outline.heading: Rituals were never cut off from the ummah
outline.gist: Once Islam becomes private rituals detached from the state of the nation of Muhammad, we fail. Zoom out of your bubble and let the bigger picture shape your intention.

outline.heading: Interlude
Reminder two: a youth-driven awakening?
outline.gist: Tickling an optimism long dead, he wonders whether the numbers show a modern awakening of young people who refuse to accept the world as it is.

outline.heading: Masjids designed to embrace the young
outline.gist: An awakening needs institutions that take young people in and harness their energy. The five-year-old who annoys you now is the fifteen-year-old you will beg to come back.

outline.heading: Every revival was led by the young
outline.gist: Check the ages of the generals, rulers and scholars we admire: many were strikingly young. The ummah has never had an awakening that was not youth-driven; elders can only support it.

outline.heading: Open minds and hearts, not just doors
outline.gist: Older generations offer wisdom, wealth and advice. The openness that matters is of mind and heart: young people arrive with good and bad habits, and a closed heart sends them away after one visit.

outline.heading: Youth talk is empty without the work
outline.gist: Unless masjids accept the bad with tenderness and patience they will not get the good. Every institution talks about youth, but the work is exhausting and often done alone.

outline.heading: Allah brought them to you: do your job
outline.gist: Mentoring is unglamorous work nobody wants, yet most of the 6,500 are young. Allah delivered them, so embrace, teach and empower them; the future is what we build today.

outline.heading: Interlude
Reminder three: dua for what He asked of you
outline.gist: Dua that pours out pain needs nothing more; it is therapeutic. But asking Allah for victory and prosperity that He commanded us to work for is a different matter.

outline.heading: An action plan: many ways to contribute
outline.gist: Without a plan for how you will contribute, the dua rings hollow. Not everyone serves politically or militarily; education, mentorship, wealth, volunteering, outreach and advocacy all count.

outline.heading: Walking where He told you to go
outline.gist: Asking Allah to do what you are too busy for is improper. A proper dua says: I am walking in the direction You told me, so grant me success.

outline.heading: Abu Hanifah and his drunk neighbour
outline.gist: A young cobbler drank nightly and sang of being neglected. When he was jailed, Abu Hanifah rode to the governor, had him and every prisoner of that night released, and rode him home in silence.

outline.heading: Did I neglect you?
outline.gist: Abu Hanifah asked only that; the young man wept, repented and became a known student whose identity was concealed. This is the mentality needed for a better future.

themes.note: Ramadan is a season when Allah calls hearts and fills the masajid; it is a push forward, and keeping the momentum after the month is the believer's responsibility.

themes.label: Intention and sincerity (niyyah, ikhlas)
themes.note: Renew your intention each Jumuah of Ramadan; find a reason, and if your relationship with Allah feels empty, make the suffering ummah part of your intention.

themes.label: Palestine, Gaza and the suffering of Muslims
themes.note: The tens of thousands killed under the rubble in Gaza did nothing wrong but share our faith and refuse to leave their land; they deserve that we do better.

themes.label: Community building, cooperation and the ummah
themes.note: Islam fails when it is reduced to private rituals cut off from the condition of the ummah; zoom out and see yourself as part of something bigger.

themes.label: Youth, their challenges and their role
themes.note: Every awakening in the ummah's history was youth-driven; the older generations can only support, advise and fund, and must invest in the young people Allah has brought.

themes.label: The masjid: its role and etiquette
themes.note: Masajid must be designed to embrace young people; the openness that matters is of mind and heart, and the annoying child who is unwelcome now will not return at fifteen.

themes.label: Dua and invocation
themes.note: Dua of complaint and sorrow needs nothing more, but dua asking Allah for what He commanded us to do needs an action plan beside it, or it becomes disrespectful.

themes.label: Mercy, forgiveness and pardoning people
themes.note: Abu Hanifah's quiet care for a sinful neighbour, and the concealment of the student's past, model the tender patience that wins people back.

quran.point: Answering Allah and His Messenger when they call to what gives spiritual life; Allah stands between a person and his heart and all will be gathered to Him.

hadith.gist: When Ramadan begins a caller calls out: seeker of good, come forward; seeker of evil, hold back.
The hearts of the servants are between two fingers of the Most Merciful; He turns them as He wills.
In Ramadan the gates of Paradise are opened, the gates of Hell are closed and the devils are chained.

maxims: Find your piece of the puzzle
Never were our rituals disconnected from the bigger picture
Zoom out of the bubble you live in
Open the doors of the mind and heart, not just the masjid
No awakening of the ummah was ever not youth driven
This type of dua requires an action plan beside it

stories.who: Prophet Muhammad's khutbahs
stories.point: His recorded khutbahs are short because his community lived year-round with the commitment we see only in Ramadan.

stories.who: Young leaders and scholars of Muslim history
stories.point: Many celebrated figures achieved their work at ages we would not trust with authority; revival always comes from the young.

stories.who: Abu Hanifah and his drunk shoemaker neighbour
stories.point: He never scolded the man, quietly got him released from prison, and asked only whether he had neglected him; the man repented and became a known scholar whose identity was concealed.

5:21.ar: يَٰقَوۡمِ ٱدۡخُلُواْ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ ٱلۡمُقَدَّسَةَ ٱلَّتِي كَتَبَ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡ وَلَا تَرۡتَدُّواْ عَلَىٰٓ أَدۡبَارِكُمۡ فَتَنقَلِبُواْ خَٰسِرِينَ
5:21.en: O my people! Go into the holy land which Allah hath ordained for you. Turn not in flight, for surely ye turn back as losers

5:22.ar: قَالُواْ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّ فِيهَا قَوۡمࣰ ا جَبَّارِينَ وَإِنَّا لَن نَّدۡخُلَهَا حَتَّىٰ يَخۡرُجُواْ مِنۡهَا فَإِن يَخۡرُجُواْ مِنۡهَا فَإِنَّا دَٰخِلُونَ
5:22.en: They said: O Moses! Lo! a giant people (dwell) therein and lo! we go not in till they go forth from thence. When they go forth from thence, then we will enter (not till then)

5:23.ar: قَالَ رَجُلَانِ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخَافُونَ أَنۡعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِمَا ٱدۡخُلُواْ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡبَابَ فَإِذَا دَخَلۡتُمُوهُ فَإِنَّكُمۡ غَٰلِبُونَۚ وَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَتَوَكَّلُوٓاْ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
5:23.en: Then out spake two of those who feared (their Lord, men) unto whom Allah had been gracious: Enter in upon them by the gate, for if ye enter by it, lo! ye will be victorious. So put your trust (in Allah) if ye are indeed believers

5:24.ar: قَالُواْ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّا لَن نَّدۡخُلَهَآ أَبَدࣰ ا مَّا دَامُواْ فِيهَا فَٱذۡهَبۡ أَنتَ وَرَبُّكَ فَقَٰتِلَآ إِنَّا هَٰهُنَا قَٰعِدُونَ
5:24.en: They said: O Moses! We will never enter (the land) while they are in it. So go thou and thy Lord and fight! We will sit here

5:25.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي لَآ أَمۡلِكُ إِلَّا نَفۡسِي وَأَخِيۖ فَٱفۡرُقۡ بَيۡنَنَا وَبَيۡنَ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلۡفَٰسِقِينَ
5:25.en: He said: My Lord! I have control of none but myself and my brother, so distinguish between us and the wrong-doing folk

5:26.ar: قَالَ فَإِنَّهَا مُحَرَّمَةٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡۛ أَرۡبَعِينَ سَنَةࣰۛ يَتِيهُونَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ فَلَا تَأۡسَ عَلَى ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلۡفَٰسِقِينَ
5:26.en: (Their Lord) said: For this the land will surely be forbidden them for forty years that they will wander in the earth, bewildered. So grieve not over the wrongdoing folk

5:32.ar: مِنۡ أَجۡلِ ذَٰلِكَ كَتَبۡنَا عَلَىٰ بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ أَنَّهُۥ مَن قَتَلَ نَفۡسَۢا بِغَيۡرِ نَفۡسٍ أَوۡ فَسَادࣲ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَكَأَنَّمَا قَتَلَ ٱلنَّاسَ جَمِيعࣰ ا وَمَنۡ أَحۡيَاهَا فَكَأَنَّمَآ أَحۡيَا ٱلنَّاسَ جَمِيعࣰ اۚ وَلَقَدۡ جَآءَتۡهُمۡ رُسُلُنَا بِٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتِ ثُمَّ إِنَّ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّنۡهُم بَعۡدَ ذَٰلِكَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ لَمُسۡرِفُونَ
5:32.en: For that cause We decreed for the Children of Israel that whosoever killeth a human being for other than manslaughter or corruption in the earth, it shall be as if he had killed all mankind, and whoso saveth the life of one, it shall be as if he had saved the life of all mankind. Our messengers came unto them of old with clear proofs (of Allah's Sovereignty), but afterwards lo! many of them became prodigals in the earth

5:82.ar: ۞لَتَجِدَنَّ أَشَدَّ ٱلنَّاسِ عَدَٰوَةࣰ لِّلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱلۡيَهُودَ وَٱلَّذِينَ أَشۡرَكُواْۖ وَلَتَجِدَنَّ أَقۡرَبَهُم مَّوَدَّةࣰ لِّلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا نَصَٰرَىٰۚ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّ مِنۡهُمۡ قِسِّيسِينَ وَرُهۡبَانࣰ ا وَأَنَّهُمۡ لَا يَسۡتَكۡبِرُونَ
5:82.en: Thou wilt find the most vehement of mankind in hostility to those who believe (to be) the Jews and the idolaters. And thou wilt find the nearest of them in affection to those who believe (to be) those who say: Lo! We are Christians. That is because there are among them priests and monks, and because they are not proud

5:100.ar: قُل لَّا يَسۡتَوِي ٱلۡخَبِيثُ وَٱلطَّيِّبُ وَلَوۡ أَعۡجَبَكَ كَثۡرَةُ ٱلۡخَبِيثِۚ فَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ يَٰٓأُوْلِي ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُفۡلِحُونَ
5:100.en: Say: The evil and the good are not alike even though the plenty of the evil attract thee. So be mindful of your duty to Allah, O men of understanding, that ye may succeed

6:8.ar: وَقَالُواْ لَوۡلَآ أُنزِلَ عَلَيۡهِ مَلَكࣱۖ وَلَوۡ أَنزَلۡنَا مَلَكࣰ ا لَّقُضِيَ ٱلۡأَمۡرُ ثُمَّ لَا يُنظَرُونَ
6:8.en: They say: Why hath not an angel been sent down unto him? If We sent down an angel, then the matter would be judged; no further time would be allowed them (for reflection)

6:9.ar: وَلَوۡ جَعَلۡنَٰهُ مَلَكࣰ ا لَّجَعَلۡنَٰهُ رَجُلࣰ ا وَلَلَبَسۡنَا عَلَيۡهِم مَّا يَلۡبِسُونَ
6:9.en: Had we appointed him (Our messenger) an angel, We assuredly had made him (as) a man (that he might speak to men); and (thus) obscured for them (the truth) they (now) obscure

5:1.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَوۡفُواْ بِٱلۡعُقُودِۚ أُحِلَّتۡ لَكُم بَهِيمَةُ ٱلۡأَنۡعَٰمِ إِلَّا مَا يُتۡلَىٰ عَلَيۡكُمۡ غَيۡرَ مُحِلِّي ٱلصَّيۡدِ وَأَنتُمۡ حُرُمٌۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَحۡكُمُ مَا يُرِيدُ
5:1.en: O ye who believe! Fulfil your indentures. The beast of cattle is made lawful unto you (for food) except that which is announced unto you (herein), game being unlawful when ye are on the pilgrimage. Lo! Allah ordaineth that which pleaseth Him

5:27.ar: ۞وَٱتۡلُ عَلَيۡهِمۡ نَبَأَ ٱبۡنَيۡ ءَادَمَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ إِذۡ قَرَّبَا قُرۡبَانࣰ ا فَتُقُبِّلَ مِنۡ أَحَدِهِمَا وَلَمۡ يُتَقَبَّلۡ مِنَ ٱلۡأٓخَرِ قَالَ لَأَقۡتُلَنَّكَۖ قَالَ إِنَّمَا يَتَقَبَّلُ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ
5:27.en: But recite unto them with truth the tale of the two sons of Adam, how they offered each a sacrifice, and it was accepted from the one of them and it was not accepted from the other. (The one) said: I will surely kill thee. (The other) answered: Allah accepteth only from those who ward off (evil)

5:28.ar: لَئِنۢ بَسَطتَ إِلَيَّ يَدَكَ لِتَقۡتُلَنِي مَآ أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطࣲ يَدِيَ إِلَيۡكَ لِأَقۡتُلَكَۖ إِنِّيٓ أَخَافُ ٱللَّهَ رَبَّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
5:28.en: Even if thou stretch out thy hand against me to kill me, I shall not stretch out my hand against thee to kill thee, lo! I fear Allah, the Lord of the Worlds

5:29.ar: إِنِّيٓ أُرِيدُ أَن تَبُوٓأَ بِإِثۡمِي وَإِثۡمِكَ فَتَكُونَ مِنۡ أَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلنَّارِۚ وَذَٰلِكَ جَزَٰٓؤُاْ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
5:29.en: Lo! I would rather thou shouldst bear the punishment of the sin against me and thine own sin and become one of the owners of the fire. That is the reward of evil-doers

5:30.ar: فَطَوَّعَتۡ لَهُۥ نَفۡسُهُۥ قَتۡلَ أَخِيهِ فَقَتَلَهُۥ فَأَصۡبَحَ مِنَ ٱلۡخَٰسِرِينَ
5:30.en: But (the other's) mind imposed on him the killing of his brother, so he slew him and became one of the losers

5:31.ar: فَبَعَثَ ٱللَّهُ غُرَابࣰ ا يَبۡحَثُ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ لِيُرِيَهُۥ كَيۡفَ يُوَٰرِي سَوۡءَةَ أَخِيهِۚ قَالَ يَٰوَيۡلَتَىٰٓ أَعَجَزۡتُ أَنۡ أَكُونَ مِثۡلَ هَٰذَا ٱلۡغُرَابِ فَأُوَٰرِيَ سَوۡءَةَ أَخِيۖ فَأَصۡبَحَ مِنَ ٱلنَّٰدِمِينَ
5:31.en: Then Allah sent a raven scratching up the ground, to show him how to hide his brother's naked corpse. He said: Woe unto me! Am I not able to be as this raven and so hide my brother's naked corpse? And he became repentant
