3LCJmaVWJG0.title: Ramadan 2024 Night 6: Quranic Reflections on Al-Ma'idah and Al-An'am
3LCJmaVWJG0.one_line: Al-Ma'idah as the contract of Islam: good versus rotten, belief without seeing angels, the sanctity of every life, misused verses, and action with dua.
3LCJmaVWJG0.summary: He presents Al-Ma'idah as the contract placed in the believer's hand: a sequence of commands that protect the five necessities and fit human nature, which Allah knows best. From 5:100 he argues that good and rotten are never equal, however flashy or popular the rotten becomes, and urges young people to judge by merit, not by numbers. From 6:8-9 he explains why angels are not sent visibly: belief means reasoning from signs, and obedience after seeing proves nothing. In 5:32, coming straight after the story of Adam's two sons, he finds the universal sanctity of life: denying it to one person denies it to all, and granting life includes jobs, health care, education and defending the oppressed. He then corrects the use of 5:82 to justify hatred: the verse tells Muslims who will see them as enemies so they can plan, not whom to hate, and an enemy is anyone who denies your right to exist, Muslim or not. He insists the Palestinian claim needs no scripture, and closes with Bani Israel at the gates of Jerusalem, warning that a community which asks Allah, or its imam, to do its work without a plan of its own repeats their mistake.

outline.heading: Opening
Al-Ma'idah puts the pen in your hand
outline.gist: After identity, method, protection and values, this surah gives the detailed terms; it has the most calls to the believers, each a command of its own.

outline.heading: The surah of covenants covers every part of life
outline.gist: Inheritance, struggle, political alliances and duties to self and nation all appear as terms of the contract.

outline.heading: The five necessities the commands protect
outline.gist: Faith, life, intellect, dignity and wealth are each safeguarded by the surah's commands.

outline.heading: Commands in keeping with human nature
outline.gist: Allah knows our urges and weaknesses; the stories of cowardice and envy in the surah show commands designed to tame the worst in us and bring out the best.

outline.heading: Why it is called the Table
outline.gist: The table of Isa's story becomes a symbol of everything Islam lays out, like putting all the cards on the table before you sign.

outline.heading: Legitimate difference versus good and rotten
outline.gist: Many matters allow several valid opinions, but the good and the rotten are never equal, and rot sits on the inside.

outline.heading: Do not be impressed by decorated rot
outline.gist: People of intellect must see past lights, abundance and strength; the rotten stays rotten whoever owns it.

outline.heading: Goodness is not decided by majority
outline.gist: Good and bad are judged objectively on merit once bias and desire are set aside, not by how many support something.

outline.heading: Stand by the good even if alone
outline.gist: Young people should learn to identify the good and hold to it even as the last person on earth who does.

outline.heading: An angel would come looking like a man
outline.gist: Seeing angels or the unseen ends belief; belief means drawing a conclusion from clues, not seeing a colour in front of you.

outline.heading: The point of the test is reasoning toward Allah
outline.gist: Reward depends on reaching Allah through signs and reason; everyone is devout on the Day of Judgment and that is not heroic.

outline.heading: Why prophets warned against demanding miracles
outline.gist: A physical sign that is rejected brings immediate destruction with no time to repent, as with the demanded she-camel.

outline.heading: Sanctity of life after the story of Adam's sons
outline.gist: The verse protecting life comes after Qabil kills his brother out of envy.

outline.heading: The first killer shares in every unjust killing
outline.gist: Whoever starts an evil banks its sin, so Adam's son bears a share of every unjust killing until the Last Day.

outline.heading: Killing one is killing all: an all-or-nothing value
outline.gist: Anyone willing to take one innocent life holds no life sacred; every human and every living thing must be respected.

outline.heading: A universal decree addressed to Bani Israel
outline.gist: The irony that the command came to Bani Israel; no person is inferior or superior in the value of their life.

outline.heading: Ways of granting life to people
outline.gist: Defending the oppressed, health care, feeding the hungry, finding someone a job, clean water and education all count as saving all humanity.

outline.heading: One human family descended from Adam
outline.gist: Placing the verse after the sons of Adam rules out limiting it to one group; then many still transgress after clear signs.

outline.heading: Who will see you as enemies, not whom to hate
outline.gist: The verse says some groups will be hostile toward believers; it is misread as a command to treat them as enemies.

outline.heading: Knowing who dislikes you helps you deal with them
outline.gist: A rational person adjusts with care toward those who dislike him; Muslims hate no one, and using the verse for an agenda is political.

outline.heading: The Jewish faith as the closest relatives
outline.gist: No two groups share more lineage, creed and law than Muslims and Jews, so they are never enemies by belief.

outline.heading: Followers of Isa and quicker alliances
outline.gist: Christians who are not arrogant will feel affinity, which tells Muslims where alliances can be built.

outline.heading: Your enemy is whoever denies your right to exist
outline.gist: Enmity is never by birth, race or belief; many such enemies are Muslim rulers who drove their people out.

outline.heading: Remember why we are on this land
outline.gist: Muslims in North America live on land taken from its first people because they could not live in their own; teach children this while respecting the land.

outline.heading: Plan accordingly and never preach hatred
outline.gist: The verse is information to plan with, and Muslims failed to plan; it must never be used for hatred.

outline.heading: Palestinian rights need no scripture
outline.gist: People who have lived in Palestine for two thousand years cannot be removed because of another people's book.

outline.heading: If ancestral claims ruled the world
outline.gist: Taken seriously, such claims would empty North America and send everyone back to ancient origins.

outline.heading: Musa at the gates of Jerusalem
outline.gist: Allah promised Bani Israel victory if they simply entered, though they were outnumbered and weaker.

outline.heading: Go you and your Lord and fight
outline.gist: Asking Allah to do what He told you to do, with no plan of your own, was rude and disrespectful toward Him.

outline.heading: Forty years lost in the wilderness
outline.gist: That generation wandered until it died out; Musa and Harun died in the wilderness after educating the generation that retook Jerusalem.

outline.heading: Critics who do not play their part
outline.gist: Community members who only critique the masjid and its imam, and duas made with no plan, come close to that same attitude.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: The purposes behind Allah's commands (maqasid)
themes.note: The surah's commands protect the five necessities and are built around the human nature Allah knows.

themes.label: Values, principles and ethics as a system
themes.note: Good and rotten are judged objectively on merit, never by popularity or how impressive the rotten looks.

themes.label: Youth, their challenges and their role
themes.note: Young people must learn to see through what looks strong and popular and stand by the good even alone.

themes.label: Eman: faith, certainty, doubt
themes.note: Belief means reasoning from signs to Allah; visible angels or miracles would end the test.

themes.label: The unlawfulness of harm and protecting others
themes.note: Every life is sacred without exception, and saving or improving one life counts as saving all humanity.

themes.label: Human equality and racism
themes.note: All people descend equally from Adam, so no life is worth less than another.

themes.label: Tolerance, pluralism and dealing with difference
themes.note: Muslims hate no one by faith or race; 5:82 is guidance for planning relations with Jews, pagans and Christians, not a call to enmity.

themes.label: Muslim identity and life in the West / Canada
themes.note: Muslims should remember they live on land taken from its first people because they were pushed out of their own.

themes.label: Palestine, Gaza and the suffering of Muslims
themes.note: The Palestinians' right to their land rests on millennia of living there, not on scriptural argument.

themes.label: Agency, responsibility and rejecting victim mentality
themes.note: Asking Allah or the imam to do the work without one's own plan or contribution repeats Bani Israel's error.

10:87.ar: وَأَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰ وَأَخِيهِ أَن تَبَوَّءَا لِقَوۡمِكُمَا بِمِصۡرَ بُيُوتࣰ ا وَٱجۡعَلُواْ بُيُوتَكُمۡ قِبۡلَةࣰ وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَۗ وَبَشِّرِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ

11:27.ar: فَقَالَ ٱلۡمَلَأُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِن قَوۡمِهِۦ مَا نَرَىٰكَ إِلَّا بَشَرࣰ ا مِّثۡلَنَا وَمَا نَرَىٰكَ ٱتَّبَعَكَ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ هُمۡ أَرَاذِلُنَا بَادِيَ ٱلرَّأۡيِ وَمَا نَرَىٰ لَكُمۡ عَلَيۡنَا مِن فَضۡلِۭ بَلۡ نَظُنُّكُمۡ كَٰذِبِينَ
11:27.en: The chieftains of his folk, who disbelieved, said: We see thee but a mortal like us, and we see not that any follow thee save the most abject among us, without reflection. We behold in you no merit above us - nay, we deem you liars

11:100.ar: ذَٰلِكَ مِنۡ أَنۢبَآءِ ٱلۡقُرَىٰ نَقُصُّهُۥ عَلَيۡكَۖ مِنۡهَا قَآئِمࣱ وَحَصِيدࣱ‏
11:100.en: That is (something) of the tidings of the townships (which were destroyed of old). We relate it unto thee (Muhammad). Some of them are standing and some (already) reaped

11:101.ar: وَمَا ظَلَمۡنَٰهُمۡ وَلَٰكِن ظَلَمُوٓاْ أَنفُسَهُمۡۖ فَمَآ أَغۡنَتۡ عَنۡهُمۡ ءَالِهَتُهُمُ ٱلَّتِي يَدۡعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مِن شَيۡءࣲ لَّمَّا جَآءَ أَمۡرُ رَبِّكَۖ وَمَا زَادُوهُمۡ غَيۡرَ تَتۡبِيبࣲ‏
11:101.en: We wronged them not, but they did wrong themselves; and their gods on whom they call beside Allah availed them naught when came thy Lord's command; they added to them naught save ruin

11:102.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ أَخۡذُ رَبِّكَ إِذَآ أَخَذَ ٱلۡقُرَىٰ وَهِيَ ظَٰلِمَةٌۚ إِنَّ أَخۡذَهُۥٓ أَلِيمࣱ شَدِيدٌ
11:102.en: Even thus is the grasp of thy Lord when He graspeth the townships while they are doing wrong. Lo! His grasp is painful, very strong

-MlYss9OVtE.title: Ramadan 2024 Night 11: Quranic Reflections on Yunus and Hud
-MlYss9OVtE.one_line: Reform as the edge of Islam's message, rejoicing in Allah's bounty, prayer and qiblah as the root of community, iman as a gift, and dawah through conduct.
-MlYss9OVtE.summary: He sets Hud's theme against Yunus's theology of decree: reform is the critical element of Islam's message, and without it Islam becomes a tame faith kept inside the masjid, which is what dictators and governments want. Drawing on Chomsky's illusion of freedom, he argues that people may debate freely inside a box whose borders are guarded, as with gender definitions or calling resistance a right of the oppressed, a form of intellectual tyranny. Each prophet confronted his people's particular corruption, and Muslims in the West must not grow comfortable with the status quo. From 10:58 he teaches that joy is allowed when blessings are seen as Allah's bounty and used as He wants. From 10:87 he shows that Musa was told to establish prayer and a direction while still persecuted, because shared prayer and the qiblah are what make a community and an ummah. From 10:99-100 he calls iman an unearned gift that cannot be coerced. From 11:27 he condemns judging people by class or a faith by its followers, then turns it on Muslims: if the community repels seekers, its conduct is the problem, since dawah works through behaviour and achievement. Hud closes with the fate of oppressive cities.

outline.heading: Opening
Take stock after the first ten nights
outline.gist: Renew intentions and review what went well and what needs fixing before the month slips away.

outline.heading: Growing in iman to serve those suffering in Gaza
outline.gist: Despite the images from Gaza, the response is to raise one's iman with the intention of serving them and to prepare for the day one can do more.

outline.heading: Interlude
Yunus and the critical point of decree
outline.gist: Each surah of this cluster tackles a point a discipline cannot do without; misunderstanding decree leads some to disbelief and others to passivity.

outline.heading: Hud: reform is the edge of the message
outline.gist: Islam identifies corruption and changes behaviour and society; remove reform and it has no bite.

outline.heading: A tame Islam inside the masjid
outline.gist: Dictators and governments, including Canada's, want an Islam that never challenges the status quo.

outline.heading: The illusion of freedom
outline.gist: Following Chomsky, he describes a box in which thought is free while its borders are presented as self-evident truths.

outline.heading: Stepping outside the box on gender
outline.gist: Muslims who question new gender definitions meet hostility and legal threat because they argue outside the permitted limits.

outline.heading: Palestine and intellectual tyranny
outline.gist: Saying resistance is the right of an oppressed people can cost a job or freedom here; intellectual tyranny ruins more in the long run than physical tyranny.

outline.heading: Each prophet faced a different corruption
outline.gist: Political, financial, ethical, entitlement, arrogance and racism: each prophet confronted what was wrong, not what already worked.

outline.heading: Reform and the world's financial system
outline.gist: A system built to enrich the rich harms the environment and education; Muslims in the West must not grow comfortable with it.

outline.heading: Interlude
Rejoice in Allah's bounty and mercy
outline.gist: The Quran never asks for a joyless life; what matters is how you view what you have.

outline.heading: Mine, or Yours that I am holding
outline.gist: Seeing blessings as from Allah changes how you use them and how you will be judged on them.

outline.heading: Better than what they gather
outline.gist: Bounty recognised as from Allah is better than everything gathered and claimed as one's own effort.

outline.heading: Houses of prayer under Pharaoh's oppression
outline.gist: Musa and Harun were told to set aside houses for worship, make them a qiblah and establish prayer while still persecuted.

outline.heading: One deen, different laws
outline.gist: Theology, values and fundamentals are the same from Adam to Muhammad; only legal details differ between prophets.

outline.heading: Prayer establishes the community
outline.gist: Without establishing salah a Muslim community does not exist.

outline.heading: Facing the House of Allah
outline.gist: Raising the hands toward the Ka'bah reconnects you to a centre; a house is where a family belongs and protects one another.

outline.heading: Without a destination, direction does not matter
outline.gist: A driver going nowhere need not care which turn he takes; only those who know where they are going plan the route.

outline.heading: You cannot be Muslim alone
outline.gist: Prayer must face the qiblah, which ties every Muslim's efforts to the betterment of one family.

outline.heading: One ummah facing one spot
outline.gist: People across the world turning to the same place unites their energy and makes one Muslim's pain another's.

outline.heading: Unity built in weakness, not strength
outline.gist: Musa's people set their direction and congregation during persecution, before they had power.

outline.heading: No soul believes except by Allah's permission
outline.gist: Iman itself is granted by Allah, which changes how we see it.

outline.heading: Enjoy the world as His bounty, or not at all
outline.gist: Enjoyment is fine if seen as His gift and used His way; he himself finds that hard and holds back.

outline.heading: Faith cannot be coerced
outline.gist: Had Allah willed, all on earth would believe, so no one can force people into iman.

outline.heading: Iman given for free
outline.gist: Born into faith without climbing mountains to find it, believers owe endless gratitude and must never treat iman as an accomplishment.

outline.heading: Four objections from Nuh's people
outline.gist: Nuh's people listed four complaints against his call.

outline.heading: Just a human like us
outline.gist: A messenger must be human so he can be emulated; the Prophet differed only in his choices and intentions.

outline.heading: Your followers are the lowest of us
outline.gist: They dismissed Nuh because former thieves, slaves and the poor followed him.

outline.heading: The evil of class arrogance
outline.gist: Dividing society into upper and lower and refusing the lower is supremacism.

outline.heading: Judge ideas, not followers; never judge people's pasts
outline.gist: Argue with a philosophy's substance rather than its adherents' behaviour, and never write people off as bad.

outline.heading: Turning the tables on ourselves
outline.gist: If Muslims repel truth-seekers, they misrepresent something beautiful and will answer for it.

outline.heading: If it worked, it would work for you
outline.gist: Non-Muslims admire Muslim family life, fasting and prayer, then look at the community's results and doubt the faith.

outline.heading: Dawah through behaviour and achievement
outline.gist: Talks only help those already on their way; actions and success are what change the world.

outline.heading: Hamzah, Umar and Sa'd ibn Mu'adh
outline.gist: The Prophet sought leaders; their conversions were celebrated, and Sa'd brought his whole clan into Islam in a single day.

outline.heading: The Throne shook for Sa'd
outline.gist: Muslim for only about seven years, Sa'd earned that honour and his influence through character and leadership.

outline.heading: Seven prophets, seven corruptions
outline.gist: Hud closes the stories of seven prophets, each facing a different challenge of reform.

outline.heading: Cities still standing and cities harvested
outline.gist: Some towns survived, others were mown down; Allah did not wrong them, they wronged themselves and their idols did not help.

outline.heading: The severe seizing of oppressive towns
outline.gist: When peoples live by oppression and injustice their end is so painful that even their enemies pity them.

outline.heading: Every oppressive regime ends in demise
outline.gist: History confirms the Quran: oppression, persecution and corruption always end in ruin.

2sZBMQSCoHw.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: Al-Wahid Al-Ahad (The One, the Only)
2sZBMQSCoHw.one_line: Al-Wahid and Al-Ahad: tawhid as the root of every name, its evidence in creation, why people dilute it, and the weight of la ilaha illa Allah.
2sZBMQSCoHw.summary: Continuing the names of domination, he presents Al-Wahid and Al-Ahad as the name from which all others are concluded and on which Islam rests: tawhid outwardly mirrored by ikhlas inwardly. He gives the Quran's argument that rival gods would contend for the throne and the heavens would collapse, then builds an observational case: the same laws govern everything from atom to galaxy, life is created by one method, the world is arranged to suit human existence, and every part of the ecosystem completes the others. Prophets came not to invent this but to point to what human nature already knows. People reject tawhid not because the argument is weak but because its consequences, service, accountability and resurrection, are heavy, so they either dilute God with many gods or inflate humans toward godhood, as in mythology and superhero stories. Shirk is attractive because many gods allow exemptions and bargaining, whereas one God means one law with no negotiation. He then recounts the virtues of la ilaha illa Allah, including the hadith of the card that outweighs ninety-nine scrolls of sins, warning that it is not a licence. Since every concept, from mercy to wisdom, is His creation, all names follow. He asks for obedience and sincerity.

outline.heading: Al-Wahid and Al-Ahad in the Quran
outline.gist: Al-Ahad appears once and Al-Wahid fifteen times, most often paired with Al-Qahhar, within the names of domination.

outline.heading: The name from which all names are concluded
outline.gist: After the name Allah, Oneness is the original attribute: no associate, no equal, and not divisible.

outline.heading: Tawhid outwardly, ikhlas inwardly
outline.gist: Islam reduced to one word is tawhid, and its inner counterpart is sincerity; both come from this name.

outline.heading: Rival gods would contend for the throne
outline.gist: If there were other gods they would compete for supremacy and the heavens and earth would collapse.

outline.heading: First evidence: the same laws everywhere
outline.gist: From atom to galaxy everything rotates around a centre and develops gradually by the same laws.

outline.heading: Second evidence: one method of creation
outline.gist: All life is produced the same way and physics is uniform across the universe; multiple creators making identical worlds would be pointless.

outline.heading: Third evidence: a world made to suit us
outline.gist: Sun, moon, rivers and mountains are arranged so that humans can exist; any different law and we would not.

outline.heading: Fourth evidence: everything completes everything else
outline.gist: The ecosystem works in a circular balance, and human tampering with it shows how fragile that balance is.

outline.heading: Prophets point to what fitrah already knows
outline.gist: Allah sent messengers to draw attention to something already in human nature; tawhid is the simplest theology.

outline.heading: Rejected for its consequences, not its weakness
outline.gist: Accepting tawhid demands change, commitment, accountability and belief in resurrection, which people dislike.

outline.heading: Diluting God by adding gods
outline.gist: Mythologies began with one figure and multiplied gods until each meant little, leading to stories of humans defying gods.

outline.heading: Inflating humans toward godhood
outline.gist: Superhero stories appeal because people want to feel unlimited.

outline.heading: One God means we are servants
outline.gist: If everything is His creation then everything serves Him, and the human ego resists that service.

outline.heading: The slave of one master and of many
outline.gist: A man answering to quarrelling bosses cannot live like one with a single master.

outline.heading: Is there a god besides Allah?
outline.gist: The verses of An-Naml ask who created, gave rain, stabilised the earth, answers the desperate and guides in darkness, demanding proof of any other god.

outline.heading: Who owns the earth? Then where is your taqwa?
outline.gist: Even idolaters admit Allah owns everything, yet keep associating partners.

outline.heading: Shirk offers flexibility and exemptions
outline.gist: One God means one law and fixed red lines; many gods and their clergy allow bargaining and exemptions.

outline.heading: Make us a god like theirs
outline.gist: Bani Isra'il wanted an idol they could work with; with Allah no one can grant an exemption from a rule, so people invent false gods.

outline.heading: La ilaha illa Allah: the key of Jannah
outline.gist: Creation was established on it; whoever makes it his last words enters Paradise.

outline.heading: The word prophets suffered for
outline.gist: Ibrahim was thrown in the fire and Zakariya and Yahya killed for this word; renew your faith by saying it, the best thing any prophet said.

outline.heading: The card that outweighs ninety-nine scrolls
outline.gist: On Judgment Day a man with vast records of sins is saved when a card bearing the shahadah outweighs them all.

outline.heading: Not a licence to live as you please
outline.gist: Such narrations show the immense value of the word, not a guarantee to rely on while neglecting deeds.

outline.heading: He defines every value
outline.gist: Since nothing existed before Him, the meanings of mercy, justice and righteousness are His creation and His to define.

outline.heading: All names follow like dominoes
outline.gist: Knowledge, power and wisdom are concepts He created, so He is the All-Knowing, All-Powerful and All-Wise.

outline.heading: Living the name: obey Him
outline.gist: Because He alone is the Creator and we are His servants, adhere to His commands.

outline.heading: Living the name: sincerity
outline.gist: Mirror outward tawhid with inner ikhlas, acting for no one else; Allah was and nothing with Him, and we return to nothing.

13:4.ar: وَفِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ قِطَعࣱ مُّتَجَٰوِرَٰتࣱ وَجَنَّٰتࣱ مِّنۡ أَعۡنَٰبࣲ وَزَرۡعࣱ وَنَخِيلࣱ صِنۡوَانࣱ وَغَيۡرُ صِنۡوَانࣲ يُسۡقَىٰ بِمَآءࣲ وَٰحِدࣲ وَنُفَضِّلُ بَعۡضَهَا عَلَىٰ بَعۡضࣲ فِي ٱلۡأُكُلِۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَعۡقِلُونَ
13:4.en: And in the Earth are neighbouring tracts, vineyards and ploughed lands, and date-palms, like and unlike, which are watered with one water. And we have made some of them to excel others in fruit. Lo! herein verily are portents for people who have sense

13:5.ar: ۞وَإِن تَعۡجَبۡ فَعَجَبࣱ قَوۡلُهُمۡ أَءِذَا كُنَّا تُرَٰبًا أَءِنَّا لَفِي خَلۡقࣲ جَدِيدٍۗ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِرَبِّهِمۡۖ وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلۡأَغۡلَٰلُ فِيٓ أَعۡنَاقِهِمۡۖ وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ أَصۡحَٰبُ ٱلنَّارِۖ هُمۡ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ
13:5.en: And if thou wonderest, then wondrous is their saying: When we are dust, are we then forsooth (to be raised) in a new creation? Such are they who disbelieve in their Lord; such have carcans on their necks; such are rightful owners of the Fire, they will abide therein

13:6.ar: وَيَسۡتَعۡجِلُونَكَ بِٱلسَّيِّئَةِ قَبۡلَ ٱلۡحَسَنَةِ وَقَدۡ خَلَتۡ مِن قَبۡلِهِمُ ٱلۡمَثُلَٰتُۗ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَذُو مَغۡفِرَةࣲ لِّلنَّاسِ عَلَىٰ ظُلۡمِهِمۡۖ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَشَدِيدُ ٱلۡعِقَابِ
13:6.en: And they bid thee hasten on the evil rather than the good, when exemplary punishments have indeed occurred before them. But lo! thy Lord is rich in pardon for mankind despite their wrong, and lo! thy Lord is strong in punishment

13:7.ar: وَيَقُولُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَوۡلَآ أُنزِلَ عَلَيۡهِ ءَايَةࣱ مِّن رَّبِّهِۦٓۗ إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ مُنذِرࣱۖ وَلِكُلِّ قَوۡمٍ هَادٍ
13:7.en: Those who disbelieve say: If only some portent were sent down upon him from his Lord! Thou art a warner only, and for every folk a guide

13:8.ar: ٱللَّهُ يَعۡلَمُ مَا تَحۡمِلُ كُلُّ أُنثَىٰ وَمَا تَغِيضُ ٱلۡأَرۡحَامُ وَمَا تَزۡدَادُۚ وَكُلُّ شَيۡءٍ عِندَهُۥ بِمِقۡدَارٍ
13:8.en: Allah knoweth that which every female beareth and that which the wombs absorb and that which they grow. And everything with Him is measured

13:9.en: He is the Knower of the Invisible and the Visible, the Great, the High Exalted

13:10.ar: سَوَآءࣱ مِّنكُم مَّنۡ أَسَرَّ ٱلۡقَوۡلَ وَمَن جَهَرَ بِهِۦ وَمَنۡ هُوَ مُسۡتَخۡفِۭ بِٱلَّيۡلِ وَسَارِبُۢ بِٱلنَّهَارِ
13:10.en: Alike of you is he who hideth the saying and he who noiseth it abroad, he who lurketh in the night and he who goeth freely in the daytime

8:32.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالُواْ ٱللَّهُمَّ إِن كَانَ هَٰذَا هُوَ ٱلۡحَقَّ مِنۡ عِندِكَ فَأَمۡطِرۡ عَلَيۡنَا حِجَارَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ أَوِ ٱئۡتِنَا بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمࣲ‏
8:32.en: And when they said: O Allah! If this be indeed the truth from Thee, then rain down stones on us or bring on us some painful doom

34:19.ar: فَقَالُواْ رَبَّنَا بَٰعِدۡ بَيۡنَ أَسۡفَارِنَا وَظَلَمُوٓاْ أَنفُسَهُمۡ فَجَعَلۡنَٰهُمۡ أَحَادِيثَ وَمَزَّقۡنَٰهُمۡ كُلَّ مُمَزَّقٍۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّكُلِّ صَبَّارࣲ شَكُورࣲ‏

fXcUresx7N4.title: Tafsir of Surat Al-Ra'd, Part 2
fXcUresx7N4.one_line: Explains 13:4-10: the diversity of life from one water, the case for resurrection, hastening punishment, demands for miracles and Allah's precise knowledge.
fXcUresx7N4.summary: He argues the Quran asks us first to respect the laws Allah uses to run the world, things we overlook because they are always there, like a child who takes his home for granted. In 13:4 neighbouring plots, vines, crops and palms all drink the same water yet differ in look and taste: one origin, diverse outcomes, pointing to one Creator. Verse 5 says the real wonder is people who see plants die and rise every day yet deny their own resurrection. Using a bloody knife as an analogy, he separates evidence from proof and asks people to keep reasoning when they look at the cosmos, where every piece is needed for life. Verse 6 shows Quraysh demanding punishment instead of good; he links this to entitlement, reminds that things can always be worse, and recalls the crippled survivors of the elephant army living in Mecca. Allah is full of forgiveness and severe in punishment, and those who see Allah as the source of law keep it even when unwatched. Verse 7 answers demands for miracles: earlier miracles broke natural laws, while the Prophet brought revelation that makes us notice them, such as the formation of a child. Verses 8-10 describe Allah's exact knowledge of every womb and every secret.

outline.heading: First respect the laws that govern the world
outline.gist: The Quran puts the laws Allah uses to run creation before the laws of fiqh, and keeps returning to rain, plants, sun, moon and mountains.

outline.heading: We take for granted what is always there
outline.gist: Like a child who never notices his warm home and family, people stop reflecting on constant phenomena that are actually the most important.

outline.heading: Simple observation teaches about Allah
outline.gist: You need no physics or biology degree; looking at how the world works tells you about Allah and yourself.

outline.heading: Neighbouring plots, vines, crops and palms
outline.gist: Seen from a plane, adjoining plots grow different things; palms that share one root and palms that stand alone show the variety of the earth.

outline.heading: One water, different tastes: oneness of origin
outline.gist: Identical soil and water produce diverse plants and flavours, a sign for people of intellect that there is one Creator.

outline.heading: From one Creator to His attributes; recap of 13:1-4
outline.gist: His other attributes follow by rigorous reasoning once a single Creator is established; he retells the meaning of the first four verses.

outline.heading: If you wonder, wonder at their denial of resurrection
outline.gist: Within years nothing of a buried body remains; deniers find a return from soil impossible.

outline.heading: Plants die and rise every day, so why not you
outline.gist: People accept a seed coming back to life after water but reject the same for themselves, though if the earth stopped producing no technology could help.

outline.heading: Science describes how, not why
outline.gist: We can describe how seeds grow but not why; science manipulates processes and does not ask the why question.

outline.heading: Chains on the necks of those who deny the obvious
outline.gist: Those who deny what keeps them alive every moment earn the Fire; we are no exception to the cycle of death and return.

outline.heading: Evidence versus proof: the bloody knife
outline.gist: Courts convict on evidence without direct proof; no one says the knife killed by itself, yet people switch off this reasoning when they look at the universe.

outline.heading: Every piece of creation is needed for life
outline.gist: Remove the sun's course, mountains, rivers or biodiversity and life would not exist; everything is lined up exactly as needed.

outline.heading: They hasten punishment before good
outline.gist: Quraysh dared the Prophet to rain stones on them, like earlier nations who sarcastically asked for things to get worse.

outline.heading: It can always be worse: entitlement and testing
outline.gist: Allah has spoiled us so we expect things to keep improving, but we are here to be tested on both sides of the seesaw.

outline.heading: Survivors of the elephant army in Mecca
outline.gist: Crippled soldiers of Abraha's army lived on in Mecca, so Quraysh knew divine punishment was real and asking for it was ignorant.

outline.heading: One of the most hopeful verses: forgiveness despite wrongdoing
outline.gist: Your Lord possesses forgiveness for people even as they wrong themselves and others, which is why they were not punished at once.

outline.heading: The Prophet's patience with Quraysh's demands
outline.gist: The seerah's negotiation period shows his patience with absurd demands and Allah's patience with His creation.

outline.heading: Whoever feels safe from punishment loses his manners
outline.gist: Allah is also severe in punishment; like an unpunished child, people test every law and exploit every loophole.

outline.heading: Seeing Allah as the source of the law
outline.gist: Those who see laws as from Allah keep them whether watched or not, unlike traffic lights treated as suggestions where no one enforces them.

outline.heading: Where is his sign? You are only a warner
outline.gist: Deniers demanded miracles like earlier prophets'; the Prophet is not an open buffet, and the signs in the first verses are already enough.

outline.heading: Miracles broke the laws; the Quran makes you observe them
outline.gist: Law-breaking miracles rarely produced lasting faith; the Prophet was given revelation and hoped for the most followers.

outline.heading: The miracle of a child's formation
outline.gist: The odds of a healthy birth and the unexplained differentiation of identical cells into placenta, ear or kidney are signs in themselves.

outline.heading: Every people has a guide
outline.gist: Allah ensures every nation has someone and something to guide it; for us it is what the coming verses describe.

outline.heading: What every womb carries: everything has its measure
outline.gist: Allah knows what wombs hold, lose or add, and everything has an appointed share of space, time and provision.

outline.heading: Even a miscarriage had its appointed existence
outline.gist: Even a pregnancy that ends unnoticed was known to Allah and given its slice of existence; nothing is pointless to Him.

outline.heading: Knower of the unseen and seen: secret and open alike
outline.gist: Whether you speak secretly or openly, move hidden at night or visible by day, it is all the same to Him.
